words.ex: He abbreviates the word 'example' as 'ex.'.
words.ex_cn: 他把单词 'example' 缩写为 'ex.'。
words.en: To abbreviate something means to make it shorter, especially by using a particular word or phrase to represent it.

words.tr: adj. 着火的；闪耀的；激动的
words.ex: The house was ablaze at night.
words.ex_cn: 那所房子在夜里着火了。
words.en: If something is ablaze, it is burning very fiercely.

words.tr:
v. 中止；中断；放弃；堕（胎）
n. 中止计划
words.ex: He decided to abort the mission because it was too dangerous.
words.ex_cn: 他决定中止任务，因为太危险了。
words.en: If an unborn baby is aborted, the pregnancy is ended deliberately and the baby is not born alive.

words.ex: The abrasion on his knee hurt a lot.
words.ex_cn: 他膝盖上的擦伤非常疼。
words.en: An abrasion is an area on a person's body where the skin has been scraped off.

words.ex: His absenteeism caused the team to lose points.
words.ex_cn: 他的缺勤导致团队丢了分数。
words.en: Absenteeism is the habitual non-presence of an employee at their job.

words.ex: He gave an absolute yes to the offer.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个提议给出了完全肯定的回答。
words.en: Absolute means complete and total, or not limited in any way.

words.ex: The house abuts the park.
words.ex_cn: 这所房子紧邻公园。
words.en: If one thing abuts another, it is next to it or touches it at one end.

words.ex: He had an accidental fall while walking.
words.ex_cn: 他在走路时不小心摔了一跤。
words.en: An accidental event happens by chance, without being planned.

words.ex: The actor received acclaim for his performance.
words.ex_cn: 这位演员因他的表演而受到赞扬。
words.en: If someone or something is acclaimed, they are praised enthusiastically and publicly.

words.tr: v. 归于；委托；授权；信任
words.ex: They accredit the discovery to the scientist.
words.ex_cn: 他们将这一发现归功于这位科学家。
words.en: To officially recognize or approve someone or something as having a particular status or meeting certain standards.

words.ex: NASA is an acronym for National Aeronautics and Space Administration.
words.ex_cn: NASA 是美国国家航空航天局的缩写。
words.en: An acronym is a word formed from the initial letters of the words in a phrase, especially when this is used as a name.

words.ex: The actual cost was lower than expected.
words.ex_cn: 实际成本比预期的低。
words.en: You use actual to emphasize that you are referring to something real or genuine.

words.ex: He is an addict who cannot stop smoking.
words.ex_cn: 他是个无法戒烟的瘾君子。
words.en: An addict is someone who is unable to stop taking harmful drugs, or someone who is very interested in something and spends a lot of time doing it.

words.ex: This food contains a harmless additive for flavor.
words.ex_cn: 这种食物含有用于调味的无害添加物。
words.en: An additive is a substance which is added in small amounts to something else in order to improve it, preserve it, or make it more effective.

words.ex: He is adept at solving math problems.
words.ex_cn: 他擅长解决数学问题。
words.en: Someone who is adept at something is very skilled at it.

words.tr:
n. 附属物；
adj. 附属的；
words.ex: The printer is an adjunct to the computer.
words.ex_cn: 打印机是电脑的附属物。
words.en: Something that is added or attached to something else but is not essential to it.

words.tr: n. 风干土坯；风干砖坯；
words.ex: The old house was built with adobe bricks.
words.ex_cn: 这栋老房子是用风干土坯砖建造的。
words.en: Adobe is a natural building material made from sand, clay, water, and some kind of fibrous or organic material (sticks, straw, and/or manure), which the builders shape into bricks using frames and dry in the sun.

words.ex: She adorned her room with flowers.
words.ex_cn: 她用鲜花装饰了房间。
words.en: To adorn something means to make it more beautiful by adding something to it.

words.ex: It is advisable to wear a helmet when riding a bike.
words.ex_cn: 骑自行车时戴头盔是明智的。
words.en: If something is advisable, it will avoid problems if you do it.

words.tr: n. 喜爱；类同；密切关系；亲和力
words.ex: She has an affinity for painting.
words.ex_cn: 她喜爱绘画。
words.en: A natural liking for or attraction to someone or something.

words.tr:
n. 总计；集合体
adj. 合计的；总的
v. （使）聚集；聚合；总计为
words.ex: The aggregate of all sales this month is $50,000.
words.ex_cn: 本月所有销售额的总计是5万美元。
words.en: An aggregate is a number of things or people that are considered as a group or a whole.

words.ex: The cat is agile and jumps high.
words.ex_cn: 这只猫很敏捷，跳得很高。
words.en: Someone who is agile can move quickly and easily.

words.ex: He had a minor ailment and stayed home from work.
words.ex_cn: 他得了一点小病，没去上班。
words.en: An ailment is a minor illness or health problem.

words.tr:
adj. 半开的；微启的
adv. 微开地；半开地
words.ex: The door was ajar so I pushed it open.
words.ex_cn: 门半开着，所以我推开了它。
words.en: If a door is ajar, it is slightly open.

words.tr: adj. 同族的；同类的；类似的
words.ex: The two stories are akin in theme.
words.ex_cn: 这两个故事在主题上是同族的。
words.en: If one thing is akin to another, it is similar to it in some way.

words.ex: The engineer checked the alignment of the wheels.
words.ex_cn: 工程师检查了车轮的对齐。
words.en: The arrangement of something in a straight line or in correct relative positions.

words.ex: The story is an allegory about kindness.
words.ex_cn: 这个故事是一个关于善良的寓言。
words.en: An allegory is a story, poem, or picture which can be interpreted to reveal a hidden meaning, typically a moral or political one.

words.ex: The big black bug bit the brave boy.
words.ex_cn: 大黑虫咬了勇敢的男孩。
words.en: Alliteration is the occurrence of the same letter or sound at the beginning of adjacent or closely connected words.

words.ex: My parents give me a weekly allowance.
words.ex_cn: 我父母每周给我零用钱。
words.en: An allowance is money that is given regularly, usually to a child, by their parents, or by the government to someone who is unemployed or ill.

words.tr: v. 暗指；（间接）提到；影射
words.ex: He alluded to the problem without naming it.
words.ex_cn: 他暗示了这个问题，但没有点明。
words.en: To allude to something means to mention it in an indirect way.

words.ex: The bird flew aloft above the trees.
words.ex_cn: 鸟儿在树顶上方高飞。
words.en: If something is aloft, it is in the air or off the ground.

words.tr:
adj. 疏远的；冷淡的
adv. 远离地
words.ex: He stayed aloof during the party.
words.ex_cn: 他在派对上保持冷淡。
words.en: Someone who is aloof is not very friendly and does not like to spend time with other people.

words.ex: The village is at an altitude of 2,000 meters.
words.ex_cn: 这个村庄的海拔是2000米。
words.en: The height of an object or point in relation to sea level or ground level.

words.ex: The restaurant has a calm ambience.
words.ex_cn: 这家餐厅有一种宁静的氛围。
words.en: The character and atmosphere of a place.

words.ex: He felt ambivalent about accepting the job offer.
words.ex_cn: 他对接受这份工作邀约感到矛盾。
words.en: If you say that someone is ambivalent about something, you mean that they have mixed feelings about it or are unsure whether they want it or not.

words.tr:
v. 缓行；溜蹄
n. 溜蹄；缓行漫步
words.ex: He amble through the park after dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他晚饭后在公园里缓行。
words.en: To walk at a slow, relaxed pace, especially for pleasure.

words.ex: He is amenable to new ideas.
words.ex_cn: 他愿意接受新想法。
words.en: If you are amenable to something, you are willing to do it or accept it.

words.tr: n. 便利设施；舒适条件；公共设施；
words.ex: The apartment has good amenities like a gym and a swimming pool.
words.ex_cn: 这套公寓有健身房和游泳池等便利设施。
words.en: An amenity is something that makes a place more pleasant or comfortable to live in.

words.ex: He stood amid the trees, quiet and still.
words.ex_cn: 他站在树木中间，安静而静止。
words.en: If something is amid other things, it is surrounded by them.

words.ex: He has amnesia and cannot remember his name.
words.ex_cn: 他患有失忆症，想不起自己的名字。
words.en: Amnesia is a medical condition that affects someone's memory and they are unable to remember events or information.

words.tr:
n. 无政府主义者
adj. 信奉无政府主义的
words.ex: He is an anarchist who hates all governments.
words.ex_cn: 他是一名无政府主义者，憎恨所有政府。
words.en: An anarchist is a person who believes in or tries to bring about anarchy.

words.ex: The students learned the anatomy of the human heart.
words.ex_cn: 学生们学习了人类心脏的解剖组织构造。
words.en: Anatomy is the study of the structure of the bodies of people or animals.

words.ex: He told an anecdote about his childhood.
words.ex_cn: 他讲了一个关于他童年的趣事。
words.en: An anecdote is a short, amusing or interesting story about a real incident or person.

words.ex: The doctor gave him anesthesia before the surgery.
words.ex_cn: 医生在手术前给他打了麻醉。
words.en: Anesthesia is the use of drugs to prevent pain during surgery or other medical procedures.

words.ex: The children love watching animated movies.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们喜欢看动画电影。
words.en: Animated means full of life or excitement, or made to appear to move as if by magic or technology.

words.ex: The house has a small annex for storage.
words.ex_cn: 这所房子有一个用于存放物品的小附属物。
words.en: To annex means to take control of a country, region, etc., especially by force; to add an area or region to a country, state, etc. : to take control of (a territory or place).

words.tr: v. 消灭；歼灭；彻底击败
words.ex: The bomb will annihilate the building.
words.ex_cn: 炸弹会摧毁那栋大楼。
words.en: To annihilate something means to destroy it completely.

words.ex: They celebrated their wedding anniversary with dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他们用晚餐庆祝结婚纪念日。
words.en: An anniversary is a date which is remembered or celebrated because a special event happened on that date in a previous year.

words.tr: n. 异常事物；反常现象；
words.ex: The strange weather this month is an anomaly.
words.ex_cn: 这个月奇怪的天气是一个异常现象。
words.en: Something that deviates from what is standard, normal, or expected.

words.tr: n. 国家或组织的法定歌曲
words.ex: The team sang the national anthem before the game.
words.ex_cn: 比赛前，球队唱了国歌。
words.en: An anthem is a song that is used to represent a particular nation, society, or group and that is sung on special occasions.

words.ex: He read an anthology of short stories last night.
words.ex_cn: 他昨晚读了一本短篇故事选集。
words.en: An anthology is a collection of writings, such as poems or stories, that have been chosen by someone because they are considered to be the best or most interesting examples of their kind.

words.ex: The doctor gave me an antibiotic for my infection.
words.ex_cn: 医生给我开了抗菌素治疗感染。
words.en: A substance that can kill or inhibit the growth of bacteria and other microorganisms.

words.ex: The old computer is antiquated and slow.
words.ex_cn: 这台旧电脑过时且缓慢。
words.en: Something that is antiquated is old-fashioned or outdated and no longer suitable for modern conditions or purposes.

words.ex: The doctor used antiseptic cream on the cut.
words.ex_cn: 医生在伤口上用了防腐药膏。
words.en: An antiseptic is a substance that prevents the growth of disease-causing microorganisms.

words.ex: The lab has a new apparatus for measuring temperature.
words.ex_cn: 实验室有一台新的温度测量装置。
words.en: The complex structure of a particular system or organization, or the equipment used for a specific purpose.

words.ex: The teacher apportioned the books equally among the students.
words.ex_cn: 老师把书平均分给了学生们。
words.en: To apportion something is to divide it and share it out among several people or things.

words.tr: adj. 水生的；水栖的；水中的；
words.ex: The fish live in aquatic plants.
words.ex_cn: 这些鱼生活在水生植物中。
words.en: Relating to water; living in or near water or taking place in water.

words.ex: The arboreal squirrel climbs high in the trees.
words.ex_cn: 这种树栖松鼠在高高的树上攀爬。
words.en: Relating to trees; living in trees.

words.ex: He is an ardent supporter of environmental protection.
words.ex_cn: 他是环境保护的热心支持者。
words.en: An ardent person has strong feelings or enthusiasm for something.

words.ex: Climbing the mountain was an arduous task.
words.ex_cn: 爬山是一项艰巨的任务。
words.en: Something that is arduous is difficult and tiring, and involves a lot of effort.

words.ex: The arid land has little rain and no trees.
words.ex_cn: 这片干旱的土地降雨稀少，没有树木。
words.en: An arid area of land has so little rain that it is very dry and cannot support much vegetation.

words.ex: The knight wore heavy armor in the battle.
words.ex_cn: 骑士在战斗中穿着沉重的盔甲。
words.en: Armor is a protective covering that is used to prevent damage from being inflicted to an object, individual, or vehicle by direct contact weapons or projectiles, usually during combat.

words.ex: The soldier walked into the armory to get a gun.
words.ex_cn: 士兵走进军械库拿了一把枪。
words.en: A place where weapons and military equipment are stored or made.

words.ex: The aroma of fresh bread filled the kitchen.
words.ex_cn: 新鲜面包的香味充满了厨房。
words.en: An aroma is a strong, pleasant smell.

words.tr: n. 兵工厂；武器库；军械库；
words.ex: The old arsenal now serves as a museum.
words.ex_cn: 这座旧兵工厂现在被用作博物馆。
words.en: An arsenal is a place where weapons and military equipment are stored or made.

words.ex: He has arthritis in his hands.
words.ex_cn: 他双手有关节炎。
words.en: Arthritis is a medical condition in which the joints in someone's body are swollen and painful.

words.tr: adj. 有抱负的；有志向的； v. “aspire”的现在分词；
words.ex: He is an aspiring writer who dreams of publishing a novel.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位有抱负的作家，梦想出版一部小说。
words.en: If you use aspiring to describe someone who is starting a particular career, you mean that they are trying to become successful in it.

words.tr: adj. 混杂的；什锦的；各样的
words.ex: He bought assorted candies at the store.
words.ex_cn: 他在商店买了各种各样的糖果。
words.en: Assorted means consisting of various kinds mixed together.

words.tr: adj. 令人震惊的；使大吃一惊的； v. “astound”的现在分词；
words.ex: The magician's trick was astounding.
words.ex_cn: 魔术师的魔术令人震惊。
words.en: If something is astounding, it is so surprising or so impressive that it is difficult to believe.

words.ex: He is an astute businessman who always makes smart decisions.
words.ex_cn: 他是个精明的商人，总是做出明智的决定。
words.en: If you describe someone as astute, you think they are clever and can see through things quickly and make good judgments.

words.ex: The leaf is asymmetrical.
words.ex_cn: 这片叶子是不对称的。
words.en: Something that is asymmetrical has two sides or halves that are different in shape, size, or style.

words.ex: He is an atheist who does not believe in God.
words.ex_cn: 他是一名不信神的无神论者。
words.en: An atheist is a person who believes that there is no God or gods.

words.ex: The muscle showed signs of atrophy after the injury.
words.ex_cn: 受伤后，肌肉出现了萎缩的迹象。
words.en: Atrophy refers to the wasting away or decrease in size of an organ or tissue, typically as a result of disease, injury, or lack of use.

words.tr: n. 依恋；附件；附加装置；
words.ex: The child showed strong attachment to his teddy bear.
words.ex_cn: 孩子对他的泰迪熊产生了强烈的依恋。
words.en: An attachment is a file that is sent along with an email message.

words.ex: He wore formal attire to the wedding.
words.ex_cn: 他穿了正式服装去参加婚礼。
words.en: Clothes, especially fine or formal ones.

words.ex: The whisper was barely audible.
words.ex_cn: 那耳语几乎听不见。
words.en: If a sound is audible, it is loud enough for you to hear it.

words.tr:
n. 试听；试唱；试演；听力
v. 试听；试音；试镜；让…试演
words.ex: He went to an audition for the school play.
words.ex_cn: 他去参加学校话剧的试听。
words.en: An audition is a short performance given by an actor, dancer, or musician so that someone can decide if they are good enough to be in a play, film, or orchestra.

words.ex: He wrote his autobiography when he was 70.
words.ex_cn: 他70岁时写了自传。
words.en: An autobiography is a book about the life of a person, written by that person.

words.tr: adj. 自动化的； v. “automate”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The factory uses automated machines to make cars.
words.ex_cn: 这家工厂使用自动化机器来制造汽车。
words.en: An automated machine or process is one that operates by itself without needing human control.

words.ex: Applications arrived in an avalanche after the job posting.
words.ex_cn: 职位发布后，申请纷至沓来。
words.en: An avalanche is a large mass of snow, ice, and rocks that falls quickly down the side of a mountain.

words.ex: He has an aversion to spicy food.
words.ex_cn: 他厌恶辛辣食物。
words.en: A strong dislike or disinclination towards someone or something.

words.ex: He is an avid reader of mystery novels.
words.ex_cn: 他热衷于阅读侦探小说。
words.en: If you say that someone is avid for something, you mean that they are very eager to get it.

words.ex: His avocation is painting on weekends.
words.ex_cn: 他的业余爱好是周末画画。
words.en: An avocation is an activity that you do because you are interested in it, rather than as your main job.

words.ex: She hires a babysitter to look after her baby.
words.ex_cn: 她请了一个保姆来照看她的宝宝。
words.en: A babysitter is someone who looks after children while their parents are out.

words.ex: He is the backbone of the team.
words.ex_cn: 他是团队的中坚。
words.en: The backbone is the most important part of something, providing support and strength.

words.ex: The actors stood in front of the backdrop with a mountain scene.
words.ex_cn: 演员们站在有山景的背景幕布前。
words.en: A backdrop is a large piece of cloth, often with scenery or buildings painted on it, that is hung at the back of a stage in a theatre.

words.ex: The fish has a sharp barb on its tail.
words.ex_cn: 这条鱼的尾巴上有一个尖锐的倒刺。
words.en: A barb is a sharp projection near the end of an arrow, fishhook, or similar object, which is angled away from the main point so as to make extraction difficult. It can also refer to a remark that is meant to hurt someone's feelings.

words.ex: The barge carried coal down the river.
words.ex_cn: 驳船沿河运送煤炭。
words.en: A barge is a long, flat-bottomed boat used for carrying freight on canals and rivers.

words.tr: n. 物物交换；实物交易；
words.ex: They used barter to trade apples for eggs.
words.ex_cn: 他们用物物交换的方式用苹果换鸡蛋。
words.en: To trade goods or services without using money.

words.ex: She threaded a bead onto the string.
words.ex_cn: 她把一颗有孔的小珠穿在绳子上。
words.en: A bead is a small piece of glass, wood, or plastic that is used for decorating clothes or making jewellery.

words.ex: The bird uses its beak to eat seeds.
words.ex_cn: 这只鸟用它的喙吃种子。
words.en: The hard, pointed, often curved part of a bird's mouth, used for picking up and eating food.

words.ex: The building is built on solid bedrock.
words.ex_cn: 这座建筑建在坚实的基岩上。
words.en: The solid rock underlying loose deposits such as soil or alluvium.

words.ex: His smile belieed his true feelings.
words.ex_cn: 他的微笑掩饰了他真实的情感。
words.en: If one thing belies another, it hides the true situation and so creates a false idea or image of someone or something.

words.tr:
n. 风箱（复数名词）
v. 怒吼；吼叫；咆哮；“bellow”的第三人称单数
n. 咆哮；怒号；“bellow”的复数
words.ex: The blacksmith pulled the bellows to make the fire hotter.
words.ex_cn: 铁匠拉风箱让火更旺。
words.en: A bellows is a device for producing a strong current of air, used especially for blowing a fire.

words.ex: The benign teacher always helped students after class.
words.ex_cn: 这位仁慈的老师总是在课后帮助学生。
words.en: A benign substance or process does not have any harmful effects.

words.ex: He left his books as a bequest to the library.
words.ex_cn: 他把他的书作为遗赠给了图书馆。
words.en: A bequest is money or property which you legally leave to someone when you die.

words.ex: The army besiege the small town.
words.ex_cn: 军队围攻这座小镇。
words.en: To surround a place with armed forces in order to capture it or force its surrender; to overwhelm someone with requests or complaints.

words.ex: The king will bestow a medal on the hero.
words.ex_cn: 国王将把奖章授予这位英雄。
words.en: To bestow something on someone means to give or present it to them.

words.ex: He drinks a cold beverage after work.
words.ex_cn: 他下班后喝一杯冷饮。
words.en: A drink, especially one other than water; a liquid for drinking.

words.ex: The two countries signed a bilateral agreement.
words.ex_cn: 这两个国家签署了一项双边协议。
words.en: Involving or affecting two parties, countries, etc.

words.ex: The soup was too bland for me.
words.ex_cn: 这汤太淡了，我不喜欢。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as bland, you mean that they are rather dull and unexciting.

words.ex: She added bleach to the white shirt to make it brighter.
words.ex_cn: 她往白衬衫里加了漂白剂，让它更亮。
words.en: To bleach something means to make it white or pale by using a chemical or by exposing it to sunlight.

words.ex: He nodded in a blink.
words.ex_cn: 他一眨眼就点了点头。
words.en: To shut and open the eyes quickly, typically involuntarily.

words.ex: A blizzard covered the town in snow.
words.ex_cn: 一场暴风雪将整个小镇覆盖在雪中。
words.en: A blizzard is a severe snowstorm with strong winds.

words.tr: n. 布鲁斯音乐；蓝色；“blue”的复数；
words.ex: He plays the blues on his guitar every evening.
words.ex_cn: 他每天晚上用吉他演奏布鲁斯音乐。
words.en: A type of slow, sad music, originally from the southern US, in which the singer typically sings about their difficult life or bad luck in love.

words.tr:
v. 虚张声势；唬人
n. 虚张声势；吓唬；峭壁
adj. 直率的
words.ex: He used a bluff to win the game.
words.ex_cn: 他用虚张声势赢得了比赛。
words.en: If you bluff, you try to make someone believe that you will do something when you do not really intend to do it, or that you know something when you do not really know it.

words.ex: Exercise can bolster your health.
words.ex_cn: 锻炼可以增强你的健康。
words.en: If you bolster something such as someone's confidence or courage, you increase it. A bolster is also a long, firm pillow.

words.ex: The gold mine became a bonanza for the town.
words.ex_cn: 这个金矿成了这个小镇的致富之源。
words.en: A bonanza is a situation or event that creates a sudden increase in wealth, good fortune, or profits.

words.ex: Clean water is a boon to the village.
words.ex_cn: 干净的水对这个村庄是有益的。
words.en: A boon is something that is very helpful and improves the quality of life.

words.tr: adj. 无聊的；令人厌倦的； v. “bore”的现在分词；
words.ex: The movie was boring.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影很无聊。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as boring, you mean that they are not interesting and make you feel tired or impatient.

words.ex: He climbed a big boulder near the river.
words.ex_cn: 他爬上了河边的一块大岩石。
words.en: A boulder is a large rounded rock.

words.ex: She bought a bouquet of flowers for her mom.
words.ex_cn: 她为妈妈买了一束花。
words.en: A bouquet is a bunch of flowers that is attractively arranged, especially one that is given to someone as a present.

words.tr:
n. 辫子；穗带
v. 编辫子；编织
words.ex: She wore a long braid down her back.
words.ex_cn: 她身后垂着一条长长的辫子。
words.en: A braid is a complex structure or pattern formed by intertwining three or more strands of flexible material such as textile fibers, wire, or hair.

words.ex: The brawl started over a simple misunderstanding.
words.ex_cn: 这场争吵源于一个简单的误解。
words.en: A brawl is a rough or noisy fight or quarrel.

words.tr:
n. 违背；
v. 攻破；
words.ex: The company committed a breach of contract.
words.ex_cn: 该公司违反了合同。
words.en: A breach of a law, rule, or agreement is an act of breaking it.

words.ex: The breakup of the team made everyone sad.
words.ex_cn: 团队的分裂让每个人都很难过。
words.en: The end of a relationship, partnership, or association.

words.ex: The view from the mountain is breathtaking.
words.ex_cn: 从山上看到的景色令人惊叹。
words.en: If you say that something is breathtaking, you mean that it is extremely beautiful or amazing.

words.ex: The sun brightens the room in the morning.
words.ex_cn: 太阳在早上使房间变亮。
words.en: To make something lighter or more colorful, or to make someone feel happier or more hopeful.

words.tr: adj. 海水的；盐水的；咸的
words.ex: The briny sea water made his skin itch.
words.ex_cn: 咸涩的海水让他的皮肤发痒。
words.en: Something that is briny is salty or contains salt, especially like sea water.

words.tr:
n. 小河；溪
v. （不）忍受；（不）容忍
words.ex: The child jumps over the brook.
words.ex_cn: 孩子跳过小溪。
words.en: A small stream; to tolerate or allow something.

words.tr:
n. 带扣；皮带扣
v. （使）搭扣扣住
words.ex: The belt has a shiny buckle.
words.ex_cn: 这条皮带有一个闪亮的带扣。
words.en: A buckle is a piece of metal or plastic attached to one end of a belt or strap, which is used to fasten it. As a verb, to buckle means to fasten something with a buckle or to bend or collapse under pressure.

words.tr: v. 迅速生长；急速增长
words.ex: The flowers burgeon in spring.
words.ex_cn: 春天时，花朵绽放。
words.en: To grow or develop quickly; to flourish.

words.tr: v. 燃烧；“burn”的现在分词； adj. 燃烧的；强烈的；
words.ex: The wood is burning in the fireplace.
words.ex_cn: 木头正在壁炉里燃烧。
words.en: A burning issue or problem is very important and needs to be dealt with immediately.

words.tr:
v. 挖洞；钻进；翻寻
n. 地洞
words.ex: The rabbit burrows under the tree.
words.ex_cn: 兔子在树下打洞。
words.en: A burrow is a hole or tunnel dug by a small animal, such as a rabbit or a mole, as a dwelling. As a verb, to burrow means to dig a hole or tunnel for habitation or refuge.

words.tr:
n. 半身像；胸部；搜捕
v. 打碎；搜捕
adj. 破产的；打碎的
words.ex: The museum has a marble bust of the ancient king.
words.ex_cn: 博物馆里有一座古代国王的大理石半身像。
words.en: A bust is a sculpture of a person's head, shoulders, and chest. As a verb, to bust means to break something, to arrest someone, or to go bankrupt.

words.ex: I took a cab to the airport.
words.ex_cn: 我打了一辆出租车去机场。
words.en: A cab is a taxi, a vehicle that carries passengers for a fare, usually calculated by a meter.

words.tr: n. 韵律；节奏；抑扬顿挫
words.ex: The dancer moved with a steady cadence.
words.ex_cn: 舞者以稳定的节奏舞动。
words.en: The rhythm or sequence of sounds or movements in speech, music, dance, etc.

words.tr: n. 校准；测定刻度；标度
words.ex: The technician did the calibration before the test.
words.ex_cn: 技术人员在测试前进行了校准。
words.en: Calibration refers to the process of checking or adjusting the accuracy of a measuring instrument or experimental procedure by comparison with a standard.

words.tr: adj. 坦率的；坦诚的；偷拍的
words.ex: He gave a candid answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了坦率的回答。
words.en: If you are candid, you are honest and say what you really think.

words.ex: The tent has a waterproof canopy.
words.ex_cn: 这顶帐篷有一个防水天篷。
words.en: A canopy is a layer of something that spreads out and covers an area, especially the branches and leaves that spread out at the top of trees in a forest.

words.ex: He believes in capitalism and owns a small business.
words.ex_cn: 他相信资本主义，并拥有一家小企业。
words.en: Capitalism is an economic system in which the means of production are privately owned and operated for profit in a competitive market.

words.ex: He took a capsule for his headache.
words.ex_cn: 他吃了一粒胶囊来缓解头痛。
words.en: A capsule is a small container or case, especially one that is sealed and contains a dose of medicine, or a spacecraft's compartment for astronauts.

words.ex: The turtle's carapace provided excellent protection.
words.ex_cn: 乌龟的甲壳提供了极好的保护。
words.en: A carapace is the hard protective shell of some animals, such as turtles and crabs.

words.tr: n. 克拉（宝石重量单位）；开（含纯金的量）
words.ex: The diamond weighs two carats.
words.ex_cn: 这颗钻石重两克拉。
words.en: A unit of weight for precious stones and pearls, equivalent to 200 milligrams.

words.ex: The cardiac patient needs to rest daily.
words.ex_cn: 这位心脏病人需要每天休息。
words.en: Cardiac means relating to the heart.

words.tr:
adj. 首要的；大红色的
n. 红衣主教；枢机主教；基数
words.ex: This is a cardinal rule in our school.
words.ex_cn: 这是我们学校的一项首要规则。
words.en: A cardinal rule or quality is the most important one.

words.ex: He made a careless mistake on the test.
words.ex_cn: 他在考试中犯了一个粗心的错误。
words.en: If you are careless, you do not pay enough attention to what you are doing, and so you make mistakes, or cause harm or damage.

words.tr:
n. 漫画；讽刺画；滑稽模仿
v. 画成漫画讽刺
words.ex: He drew a caricature of the teacher with big eyes.
words.ex_cn: 他画了一幅老师大眼睛的漫画。
words.en: A caricature is a drawing or description of someone that exaggerates their appearance or behavior in a humorous or critical way.

words.ex: We went to the carnival last weekend.
words.ex_cn: 我们上周末去了嘉年华。
words.en: A carnival is a public festival, typically one held annually in a particular place, involving processions, music, and dancing.

words.ex: The lion is a carnivorous animal.
words.ex_cn: 狮子是一种食肉动物。
words.en: Carnivorous animals or plants eat meat.

words.ex: The enzyme acts as a catalyst in the reaction.
words.ex_cn: 这种酶在反应中充当催化剂。
words.en: A catalyst is a substance that increases the rate of a chemical reaction without itself undergoing any permanent chemical change. In a broader sense, it can also refer to a person or thing that precipitates a change.

words.ex: The earthquake was a catastrophe.
words.ex_cn: 这场地震是一场灾难。
words.en: An event causing great and often sudden damage or suffering; a disaster.

words.ex: The cat is catching a mouse.
words.ex_cn: 猫正在捉一只老鼠。
words.en: If an illness or a disease is catching, it can be passed from one person to another through touch or through the air. If a mood or an idea is catching, it spreads quickly from one person to another.

words.ex: The children explored a dark cavern.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们探索了一个黑暗的洞穴。
words.en: A cavern is a large cave or a large chamber in a cave.

words.tr: adj. 天空的；天体的；天国的；
words.ex: The celestial lights shone brightly in the night sky.
words.ex_cn: 天空中的光芒在夜空中明亮地闪耀。
words.en: Relating to the sky or the heavens; belonging or relating to heaven as the abode of the gods.

words.tr:
adj. 一百年的
n. 百年纪念
words.ex: The city held a centennial parade to celebrate 100 years.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市举行了一场百年游行来庆祝一百周年。
words.en: A centennial is the one-hundredth anniversary of an event, or something that happens every hundred years.

words.ex: He wore a ceremonial robe for the wedding.
words.ex_cn: 他为婚礼穿了一件仪式性的长袍。
words.en: relating to or used in a ceremony; formal

words.tr:
v. 摩擦；擦痛；惹怒
n. 擦伤；激怒
words.ex: His socks chafe his ankles.
words.ex_cn: 他的袜子磨得脚踝疼。
words.en: If skin chafes, it becomes sore because something is rubbing against it; to feel impatient or irritated.

words.ex: He felt chagrin when he lost the game.
words.ex_cn: 他输掉比赛时感到懊恼。
words.en: Chagrin is a feeling of disappointment, upset, or annoyance, perhaps because of your own failure.

words.tr: adj. 贞洁的；忠贞的；朴素的
words.ex: She remained chaste despite the pressure.
words.ex_cn: 尽管有压力，她依然保持贞洁。
words.en: If you describe someone as chaste, you mean that they do not have sex with anyone, or they only have sex with their husband or wife.

words.ex: The chef cooked a delicious dinner for the guests.
words.ex_cn: 主厨为客人做了一顿美味的晚餐。
words.en: A chef is a professional cook, typically the chief cook in a restaurant or hotel.

words.tr:
n. 凿子
v. 雕；凿；欺骗
words.ex: He used a chisel to carve the stone.
words.ex_cn: 他用凿子雕刻石头。
words.en: A chisel is a tool with a long metal blade which has a sharp edge for cutting wood, stone, or metal.

words.tr: n. 骑士精神；骑士制度；
words.ex: He showed chivalry by helping the lady carry her bags.
words.ex_cn: 他帮助那位女士提包，展现了骑士精神。
words.en: Chivalry is a set of qualities such as bravery, courtesy, honor, and gallantry toward women, associated with the medieval institution of knighthood.

words.tr: n. 令人讨厌的或繁重的工作；
words.ex: Washing dishes is a boring chore.
words.ex_cn: 洗碗是一件烦人的琐事。
words.en: A chore is a task or piece of work that is often boring or unpleasant but needs to be done regularly.

words.tr: n. 编舞艺术；舞蹈编排；
words.ex: The dancer praised the choreography of the ballet.
words.ex_cn: 这位舞者称赞了这部芭蕾舞的编舞艺术。
words.en: Choreography is the art of designing sequences of movements in which motion, form, or both are specified. Choreography may also refer to the design itself. A choreographer is one who creates choreographies by practicing the art of choreography.

words.ex: The chubby baby laughed loudly.
words.ex_cn: 那个胖乎乎的宝宝大声笑了。
words.en: Someone who is chubby is slightly fat in a way that people often find attractive.

words.ex: He ate a chunk of cheese for lunch.
words.ex_cn: 他午餐吃了一大块奶酪。
words.en: A chunk of something is a large piece or amount of it.

words.ex: He drank a glass of cider at the farm party.
words.ex_cn: 他在农场聚会上喝了一杯苹果酒。
words.en: Cider is an alcoholic drink made from apples, or a non-alcoholic drink made from apples which is similar to apple juice.

words.ex: He cracked the cipher to find the secret message.
words.ex_cn: 他破解了密码，找到了秘密信息。
words.en: A cipher is a secret or disguised way of writing; a code. It can also refer to a person or thing of no importance.

words.ex: The law circumscribes what companies can do.
words.ex_cn: 法律限制了公司能做的事情。
words.en: To circumscribe something means to limit its size, activity, or scope, often by setting boundaries or restrictions.

words.ex: He applied for citizenship last year.
words.ex_cn: 他去年申请了公民身份。
words.en: Citizenship is the status of being a citizen of a particular country.

words.ex: The civilian population stayed safe during the conflict.
words.ex_cn: 平民在冲突期间保持安全。
words.en: A civilian is a person who is not a member of the military or of a police or firefighting force.

words.tr:
n. 喧嚷；大声的要求
v. 喧嚷；大声地要求
words.ex: The crowd made a loud clamor for justice.
words.ex_cn: 人群为正义发出大声喧哗。
words.en: If people are clamoring for something, they are demanding it in a noisy or angry way.

words.ex: The clan lived in a small village for centuries.
words.ex_cn: 这个氏族几个世纪以来一直住在一个小村庄里。
words.en: A clan is a group of families or relatives who are connected by blood or marriage and who often share the same surname.

words.tr:
v. 鼓掌；拍手
n. 鼓掌；拍手
words.ex: The crowd will clap after the song.
words.ex_cn: 歌曲结束后，观众会鼓掌。
words.en: To clap means to strike the palms of your hands together to show appreciation or to make a noise.

words.ex: The clergy prayed in the church every morning.
words.ex_cn: 神职人员每天早上在教堂祈祷。
words.en: The clergy are the official leaders of religious activities in certain religions, especially in Christianity.

words.ex: The hiker stood at the edge of the cliff.
words.ex_cn: 徒步者站在悬崖边上。
words.en: A cliff is a high area of rock with a very steep side, often at the edge of the sea or a river.

words.tr:
n. 厚木底皮鞋；木屐
v. 堵塞；妨碍
words.ex: She wore wooden clogs to work in the garden.
words.ex_cn: 她穿着厚木底皮鞋去花园干活。
words.en: If something clogs a hole or place, it blocks it so that nothing can pass through.

words.tr: v. 聚合；合并；长到一起
words.ex: The small ponds coalesce into a large lake.
words.ex_cn: 小池塘合并成一个大湖。
words.en: If two or more things coalesce, they come together and form a single group or system.

words.ex: The two parties formed a coalition to win the election.
words.ex_cn: 这两个政党联合起来以赢得选举。
words.en: A coalition is a temporary alliance for combined action, especially of political parties forming a government.

words.tr: v. 哄；用好话劝诱；哄骗
words.ex: He tried to coax the cat out from under the bed.
words.ex_cn: 他试图哄猫从床底下出来。
words.en: To coax someone means to persuade them to do something by gentle persuasion or flattery.

words.ex: Cats and dogs can coexist in the same house.
words.ex_cn: 猫和狗可以在同一个房子里共存。
words.en: To exist together at the same time or in the same place.

words.tr:
adj. 集体的；
n. 集体；
words.ex: The collective decision was made by all members.
words.ex_cn: 这个集体决定是由所有成员做出的。
words.en: done or shared by all members of a group of people

words.ex: He uses colloquial words when talking with friends.
words.ex_cn: 他和朋友聊天时使用口语化的词语。
words.en: Colloquial language is informal language that is used in ordinary conversation rather than in writing or formal speech.

words.ex: The statue was colossal, taller than the building.
words.ex_cn: 这座雕像巨大，比大楼还高。
words.en: If you describe something as colossal, you are emphasizing that it is very large.

words.tr:
adj. 易燃的；燃烧性的；易激动的
n. 燃质物；可燃物
words.ex: The wood is combustible and burns easily.
words.ex_cn: 这种木头是可燃的，容易燃烧。
words.en: A combustible material or gas catches fire and burns easily.

words.tr:
n. 连环漫画；
adj. 滑稽的；
words.ex: He reads a comic every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上读一本连环漫画。
words.en: A comic is someone who entertains people by making them laugh, especially a professional comedian.

words.tr: adj. 群体的；社区的；公有的；
words.ex: They share a communal kitchen.
words.ex_cn: 他们共用一个群体厨房。
words.en: Communal means relating to or shared by all the members of a community.

words.tr: adj. 令人信服的； v. “compel”的现在分词；
words.ex: His story was compelling and made everyone listen.
words.ex_cn: 他的故事令人信服，让所有人都认真聆听。
words.en: A compelling argument or reason is one that makes you believe it or accept it because it is so strong.

words.tr: adj. 自满的；自鸣得意的
words.ex: He is complacent about his good grades.
words.ex_cn: 他对自己的好成绩感到自满。
words.en: A complacent person is very pleased with themselves or feels that they do not need to do anything about a situation, even though the situation may be uncertain or dangerous.

words.ex: He was accused of complicity in the theft.
words.ex_cn: 他被指控参与了这起盗窃案。
words.en: Complicity is involvement with other people in an illegal activity or wrongdoing.

words.ex: The hotel gave us complimentary breakfast.
words.ex_cn: 酒店免费赠送了我们早餐。
words.en: If something is complimentary, it is given or done free of charge. It can also mean expressing a compliment; praising or approving.

words.ex: He cannot comprehend the simple math problem.
words.ex_cn: 他无法理解这个简单的数学问题。
words.en: To comprehend something means to understand it fully.

words.ex: The spoon has a concave surface.
words.ex_cn: 勺子有一个凹的表面。
words.en: A concave surface is curved inward, like the inside of a bowl.

words.ex: The circles are concentric and share the same center.
words.ex_cn: 这些圆是同心的，拥有同一个中心。
words.en: Having a common center, as circles or spheres.

words.tr: adj. 无可置疑的；决定性的；
words.ex: The evidence was conclusive.
words.ex_cn: 证据是无可置疑的。
words.en: If something is conclusive, it means that it proves something in a way that is certain and leaves no doubt.

words.ex: The rain was a concomitant of the storm.
words.ex_cn: 雨水是这场风暴的同时发生的事。
words.en: Something that is concomitant with something else, especially something undesirable, happens at the same time as it or is connected with it.

words.ex: Two events happen concurrently.
words.ex_cn: 两个事件同时发生。
words.en: Happening or existing at the same time.

words.ex: She added ketchup as a condiment to her fries.
words.ex_cn: 她把番茄酱当作调味品加在薯条上。
words.en: A condiment is a substance such as salt, pepper, or mustard that you add to food when you eat it in order to improve the flavor.

words.ex: The two countries formed a confederate alliance to defend their borders.
words.ex_cn: 这两个国家结成了同盟联盟以保卫它们的边界。
words.en: A confederate is someone who works with others to achieve a common goal, often in a political or military context. It can also refer to a member of a confederation, which is a union of states or groups united for a common purpose.

words.ex: She confides in her best friend.
words.ex_cn: 她向最好的朋友倾诉。
words.en: If you confide in someone, you tell them a secret.

words.ex: The confluence of the two rivers created a fertile valley.
words.ex_cn: 两条河流的汇流形成了一个肥沃的山谷。
words.en: The confluence of two or more things is the junction or merging of them, often forming something greater or more complex.

words.ex: The weather was congenial for a picnic.
words.ex_cn: 天气非常适合野餐。
words.en: A congenial person, place, or environment is pleasant because it suits your character or nature.

words.ex: Traffic congestion caused delays on the highway.
words.ex_cn: 交通堵塞导致了高速公路的延误。
words.en: Congestion refers to the state of being overcrowded, especially with traffic or people, or the condition of being blocked or clogged.

words.ex: People congregate in the park on weekends.
words.ex_cn: 人们在周末聚集在公园里。
words.en: To congregate means to come together in a group or crowd.

words.ex: His conjecture was that the missing key was in the drawer.
words.ex_cn: 他猜测丢失的钥匙在抽屉里。
words.en: A conjecture is a conclusion that is based on information that is not certain or complete.

words.ex: He is a connoisseur of fine wine.
words.ex_cn: 他是优质葡萄酒的行家。
words.en: A connoisseur is a person who is especially competent to pass critical judgments in an art, particularly one of the fine arts, or in matters of taste.

words.ex: The letter 'b' is a consonant.
words.ex_cn: 字母 'b' 是一个辅音。
words.en: A consonant is a speech sound that is articulated with complete or partial closure of the vocal tract.

words.tr:
n. （统治者的）配偶；一组
v. 厮混；结交
words.ex: The king walked with his consort at the parade.
words.ex_cn: 国王在游行中与他的配偶一起行走。
words.en: A consort is a husband or wife, especially of a reigning monarch. As a verb, it means to habitually associate with someone, typically with the implication of a close or intimate relationship.

words.ex: They believed there was a conspiracy to hide the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他们相信有人密谋隐瞒真相。
words.en: A conspiracy is a secret plan by a group of people to do something harmful or illegal.

words.tr: n. 星座；一群杰出人物；一系列（相关的想法、事物）
words.ex: He saw the Orion constellation in the night sky.
words.ex_cn: 他在夜空中看到了猎户座。
words.en: A constellation is a group of stars which form a pattern and have a name.

words.ex: The snake constricts its prey.
words.ex_cn: 蛇缠住它的猎物。
words.en: If something constricts you, it limits your actions so that you cannot do what you want to do.

words.tr: adj. 传染性的；有感染力的；
words.ex: The flu is contagious and spreads easily.
words.ex_cn: 流感具有传染性，容易传播。
words.en: A contagious disease can be caught by touching someone who has the disease or by touching an infected object or by breathing in infected air.

words.tr: adj. 相接的；相邻的；接壤的
words.ex: The two countries are contiguous.
words.ex_cn: 这两个国家是相邻的。
words.en: Being in contact; touching or next to each other.

words.ex: The colors from red to violet form a continuum.
words.ex_cn: 从红色到紫色的颜色构成一个连续体。
words.en: A continuum is a continuous sequence in which adjacent elements are not perceptibly different from each other, although the extremes are quite distinct.

words.tr:
n. 轮廓；外形；等高线
v. 画轮廓（画等高线）
adj. 显示轮廓的
words.ex: The map shows the contour of the mountain.
words.ex_cn: 这张地图显示了山的轮廓。
words.en: The outline of a figure, body, or mass, especially the curved shape of a surface.

words.ex: The ball has a convex surface.
words.ex_cn: 这个球有一个凸出的表面。
words.en: A convex surface curves outward in the middle.

words.tr: adj. 欢乐的；轻松快活的；好交际的
words.ex: The party was convivial and everyone laughed a lot.
words.ex_cn: 派对气氛友好愉快，大家都笑得很开心。
words.en: A convivial atmosphere or event is friendly and pleasant, and people enjoy being together.

words.tr: adj. 全世界的；四海一家的；
words.ex: This city has a cosmopolitan population.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市有着来自世界各地的人口。
words.en: A cosmopolitan place or society is full of people from many different countries and cultures.

words.ex: Wear a helmet to counteract the risk of head injury.
words.ex_cn: 戴头盔以对抗头部受伤的风险。
words.en: If you counteract something, you reduce its effect by doing something that produces an opposite effect.

words.ex: He tried to counterfeit money.
words.ex_cn: 他试图伪造货币。
words.en: Made in exact imitation of something valuable with the intention to deceive or defraud.

words.tr: adj. 无数的；多的；数不清的；
words.ex: There are countless stars in the night sky.
words.ex_cn: 夜空中有无数颗星星。
words.en: Too numerous to count.

words.ex: The courier delivered the letter quickly.
words.ex_cn: 信使迅速送来了这封信。
words.en: A courier is a person or company that delivers messages, packages, and mail.

words.ex: The case will be heard in court next week.
words.ex_cn: 这个案件将于下周在法院审理。
words.en: A court is a place where legal matters are decided by a judge and jury or by a magistrate.

words.tr:
v. 包括；遮盖；报道；
n. 遮盖物；庇护所；封面；
words.ex: The book covers basic math and science.
words.ex_cn: 这本书包括基础数学和科学。
words.en: If something covers something else, it has been placed over or upon it, usually in order to protect it or hide it.

words.ex: The cowhand rides a horse to herd cattle.
words.ex_cn: 牧人骑马放牧牛群。
words.en: A cowhand is a person who works on a ranch, especially one who looks after cattle.

words.ex: The little cabin is cozy and warm.
words.ex_cn: 这座小木屋舒适又温暖。
words.en: A place that is cozy is comfortable and warm.

words.ex: He crammed the suitcase with clothes.
words.ex_cn: 他把衣服塞满了行李箱。
words.en: If you cram things or people into a place, you put them into it even though there is hardly enough room for them.

words.ex: The bomb left a deep crater in the road.
words.ex_cn: 炸弹在道路上炸出了一个深深的弹坑。
words.en: A crater is a large hole in the ground, typically caused by an explosion or the impact of a meteorite.

words.ex: The child drew a sun with a red crayon.
words.ex_cn: 孩子用红色蜡笔画了一个太阳。
words.en: A crayon is a stick of colored wax used for drawing or coloring.

words.ex: He showed his credentials to get the job.
words.ex_cn: 他展示了资历来获得这份工作。
words.en: Credentials are documents that prove your identity or qualifications.

words.ex: The children played near the creek after school.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们放学后在小河旁玩耍。
words.en: A creek is a small, narrow stream or river.

words.ex: The small plant grew in a crevice of the rock.
words.ex_cn: 这棵小植物长在岩石的裂隙里。
words.en: A crevice is a narrow crack or gap, especially in a rock.

words.tr: adj. 深红色的；绯红色的；
words.ex: The sky turned crimson at sunset.
words.ex_cn: 日落时，天空变成了深红色。
words.en: A deep red color that is slightly purplish, often associated with blood or a blush.

words.tr:
adj. 十字形的；交叉的
adv. 十字形地；交叉着
v. 划十字；纵横交错
words.ex: The criss-cross lines on the paper made a net.
words.ex_cn: 纸上的十字形线条形成了一个网。
words.en: To move back and forth over something, or to mark something with lines that cross each other.

words.ex: The teacher will critique the student's essay tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 老师明天会对学生的作文发表评论。
words.en: A critique is a detailed analysis and assessment of something, especially a literary, philosophical, or political theory.

words.tr:
adj. 弯曲的；扭曲的；欺诈的；不老实的
v. （使）弯曲；使成钩状；“crook”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: The path was crooked and hard to walk on.
words.ex_cn: 这条路是弯曲的，很难走。
words.en: If you describe something as crooked, especially something that is usually straight, you mean that it is bent or twisted.

words.ex: The old wall began to crumble after the rain.
words.ex_cn: 旧墙在雨后开始坍塌。
words.en: If something crumbles, or if you crumble it, it breaks into a lot of small pieces.

words.ex: He crumpled the paper in his hand.
words.ex_cn: 他把纸揉皱了。
words.en: If you crumple something such as paper or cloth, or if it crumples, it is squashed and becomes full of untidy creases and folds.

words.ex: He has a culinary degree from a famous school.
words.ex_cn: 他从一所著名学校获得了烹饪学位。
words.en: Relating to cooking or the kitchen.

words.ex: The old system is cumbersome and slow.
words.ex_cn: 这个旧系统复杂而低效。
words.en: Something that is cumbersome is large and heavy and therefore difficult to carry, wear, or handle.

words.ex: The curator arranged the paintings in the museum.
words.ex_cn: 馆长在博物馆里布置了这些画作。
words.en: A curator is someone who is in charge of the objects or works of art in a museum or art gallery.

words.ex: The old man muttered a curse under his breath.
words.ex_cn: 老人低声嘟囔了一句诅咒。
words.en: A curse is a word or sentence that is used to wish evil or harm on someone or something.

words.ex: She put a cushion on the chair to make it comfortable.
words.ex_cn: 她在椅子上放了一个靠垫，让它更舒服。
words.en: A cushion is a soft bag of some ornamental material, stuffed with wool, hair, feathers, polyester staple fiber, non-woven material, or even paper torn into fragments. It may be used for sitting or kneeling upon, or to soften the hardness or angularity of a chair or couch.

words.tr: n. 管理人；保管人；监护人
words.ex: The custodian takes care of the school building.
words.ex_cn: 管理人负责照顾学校大楼。
words.en: A custodian is someone who is responsible for looking after or protecting something valuable or important.

words.ex: He drew a dagger from his belt.
words.ex_cn: 他从腰带上抽出一把匕首。
words.en: A dagger is a weapon like a very short sword, used for stabbing.

words.ex: She picked a white daisy in the field.
words.ex_cn: 她在田野里摘了一朵白色的雏菊。
words.en: A daisy is a small wild flower with white petals and a yellow center.

words.tr: adj. 大胆的；勇敢的； v. “dare”的现在分词；
words.ex: He made a daring jump off the bridge.
words.ex_cn: 他大胆地从桥上跳了下去。
words.en: If you describe a person or their behaviour as daring, you mean that they are willing to do things which might be dangerous or which might shock or anger other people.

words.tr:
v. （使）突然移动；快速投掷；
n. 镖；
words.ex: The cat darted across the room.
words.ex_cn: 猫突然冲过房间。
words.en: A dart is a small, narrow object with a sharp point which can be thrown or shot. It can also mean to move suddenly and quickly in a particular direction.

words.tr: v. 追溯到；“date”的过去式和过去分词； adj. 过时的；陈旧的；
words.ex: This coin is dated to the year 1500.
words.ex_cn: 这枚硬币追溯到1500年。
words.en: Something that is dated is old-fashioned and no longer relevant or useful.

words.tr: adj. 使人畏缩的；吓人的； v. “daunt”的现在分词；
words.ex: The math test seemed daunting to him.
words.ex_cn: 这次数学考试让他感到畏缩。
words.en: Something that is daunting makes you feel slightly afraid or worried about dealing with it.

words.ex: It is debatable whether he is the best player.
words.ex_cn: 他是不是最好的球员是有争议的。
words.en: If you say that something is debatable, you mean that it is not certain whether it is true or right.

words.ex: The storm left debris on the road.
words.ex_cn: 风暴在道路上留下了碎片。
words.en: The remains of something that has been destroyed or broken up.

words.tr: adj. 堕落的；颓废的；衰落的
words.ex: He ate a decadent chocolate cake.
words.ex_cn: 他吃了一块奢华的巧克力蛋糕。
words.en: If you describe a person or their behavior as decadent, you think that they are morally corrupt or that they are living in an immoral way.

words.ex: The deceptive smile hid his true intentions.
words.ex_cn: 那欺骗性的微笑隐藏了他真正的意图。
words.en: If something is deceptive, it encourages you to believe something which is not true.

words.tr: adj. 每年落叶的；定期脱落的；非永久性的
words.ex: The trees lose their leaves in autumn because they are deciduous.
words.ex_cn: 这些树在秋天落叶，因为它们是落叶的。
words.en: Deciduous trees or plants lose their leaves in autumn or the dry season.

words.ex: He defecated after eating breakfast.
words.ex_cn: 他吃完早餐后排便了。
words.en: To defecate means to discharge feces from the body.

words.ex: He will defer his trip until next month.
words.ex_cn: 他将把旅行推迟到下个月。
words.en: If you defer an event or action, you arrange for it to happen at a later date, rather than immediately or at the previously planned time.

words.tr: adj. 决定性的；权威性的；确定的；
words.ex: The test results were definitive.
words.ex_cn: 这些检测结果是决定性的。
words.en: A definitive book, performance, or report is considered to be the best of its kind that has ever been done or that will ever be done.

words.ex: The heat made the metal deform.
words.ex_cn: 热量使金属变形。
words.en: To deform something means to change its shape, usually in a way that makes it less attractive or useful.

words.ex: The chef made a deft cut with the knife.
words.ex_cn: 厨师用刀熟练地切了一下。
words.en: A deft action is skilful and often quick.

words.ex: The sun can dehydrate your skin quickly.
words.ex_cn: 太阳会很快使你的皮肤脱水。
words.en: To dehydrate something means to remove all the water from it, often in order to preserve it. If you dehydrate, you lose too much water from your body, usually because of illness or extreme heat.

words.ex: He did not deign to answer her question.
words.ex_cn: 他不屑于回答她的问题。
words.en: If someone deigns to do something, they do it unwillingly and with a feeling of superiority.

words.ex: The ancient people worshipped a sun deity.
words.ex_cn: 古人崇拜太阳神。
words.en: A deity is a god or goddess, or anything revered as divine.

words.tr: adj. 美味的；使人愉快的
words.ex: The cake was delectable.
words.ex_cn: 这个蛋糕非常美味。
words.en: If you describe something, especially food or drink, as delectable, you mean that it is very pleasant.

words.tr: n. 精神错乱；谵妄；极度兴奋
words.ex: The patient was in a state of delirium after the surgery.
words.ex_cn: 手术后，病人处于精神错乱的状态。
words.en: A state of wild excitement or mental confusion, often accompanied by hallucinations.

words.ex: The Nile River forms a large delta before it flows into the sea.
words.ex_cn: 尼罗河在流入大海之前形成了一个巨大的三角洲。
words.en: A delta is an area of low, flat land shaped like a triangle, where a river splits and spreads out into several branches before entering the sea.

words.tr: v. 遣散；（使）复员；使退伍
words.ex: The army will demobilize after the war ends.
words.ex_cn: 战争结束后，军队将解散。
words.en: To demobilize is to release someone from military service, especially at the end of a war.

words.ex: They will demolish the old building next week.
words.ex_cn: 他们下周会拆掉那座旧建筑。
words.en: To demolish something such as a building means to destroy it completely. It can also mean to defeat someone completely in a discussion, argument, or competition.

words.ex: There are many denominations in Christianity.
words.ex_cn: 基督教中有许多宗派。
words.en: A denomination is a recognized autonomous branch of the Christian Church or a unit of value, especially in currency.

words.ex: The scandal caused a dent in his reputation.
words.ex_cn: 这场丑闻削弱了他的声誉。
words.en: A dent is a hollow or depression in a surface, often caused by a blow or pressure.

words.ex: He wants to study dentistry after high school.
words.ex_cn: 他想在高中毕业后学习牙科。
words.en: Dentistry is the profession or science concerned with the prevention and treatment of diseases and disorders of the teeth and gums.

words.ex: The drought depletes the water supply.
words.ex_cn: 干旱耗尽了水源。
words.en: If you deplete something, you reduce the amount of it that is available or that exists.

words.ex: The trucks stop at the depot to load goods.
words.ex_cn: 卡车在仓库停靠以装载货物。
words.en: A depot is a place where large amounts of raw materials, manufactured goods, or equipment are stored until they are needed.

words.ex: The car's depreciation is high after five years.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车五年后折旧很高。
words.en: A decrease in the value of a currency with respect to other currencies or a decrease in the value of an asset over time due to wear and tear, obsolescence, or age.

words.ex: The depredation of forests harms wildlife.
words.ex_cn: 森林的破坏危害了野生动物。
words.en: The act of preying upon or plundering; the act of laying waste; as, the depredations of an army on the country.

words.ex: The deputy signed the document for the manager.
words.ex_cn: 代理人替经理签署了文件。
words.en: A deputy is a person who is appointed to act as a substitute for another, especially in a position of authority.

words.ex: The plant uses desalination to make seawater drinkable.
words.ex_cn: 该工厂使用脱盐作用将海水变为可饮用水。
words.en: The process of removing salt from seawater to make it suitable for drinking or irrigation.

words.ex: The desert looks desolate and empty.
words.ex_cn: 这片沙漠看起来荒凉而空旷。
words.en: If you describe a place as desolate, you mean that it is empty and looks sad because there are no people there or because it has been damaged.

words.tr: v. 抢劫；掠夺；蹂躏；破坏
words.ex: The invaders despoiled the village.
words.ex_cn: 入侵者抢劫了村庄。
words.en: To despoil something means to steal from it or damage it, especially in a violent or destructive way.

words.ex: The high fine will deter people from breaking the law.
words.ex_cn: 高额罚款会制止人们违法。
words.en: If something deters you from doing something, it makes you not want to do it or continue doing it.

words.tr: n. 洗涤剂；洗衣粉；去垢剂；
words.ex: She uses detergent to wash the clothes.
words.ex_cn: 她用洗涤剂洗衣服。
words.en: A detergent is a substance that is used for cleaning things, especially clothes and dishes.

words.ex: The weather is a determinant of whether we go hiking.
words.ex_cn: 天气是我们是否去远足的决定因素。
words.en: A determinant is a factor which decisively affects the nature or outcome of something.

words.ex: He detests eating broccoli.
words.ex_cn: 他讨厌吃西兰花。
words.en: If you detest something, you dislike it intensely.

words.ex: Smoking is detrimental to your health.
words.ex_cn: 吸烟对你的健康有害。
words.en: Something that is detrimental has a harmful or damaging effect on something else.

words.ex: The earthquake devastated the small town.
words.ex_cn: 地震摧毁了这个小镇。
words.en: To devastate means to destroy or ruin something completely, or to cause someone to feel extreme sadness or shock.

words.ex: The room was devoid of any furniture.
words.ex_cn: 这个房间里全无家具。
words.en: If you say that someone or something is devoid of a quality or thing, you are emphasizing that they have none of it.

words.tr: v. 吞食；吞噬；狼吞虎咽地吃；如饥似渴地看
words.ex: The dog devoured the meat quickly.
words.ex_cn: 狗很快地把肉吃光了。
words.en: To eat something quickly and eagerly, especially because you are very hungry; to destroy something quickly and completely.

words.tr:
adj. 对角线的；斜的
n. 对角线；斜线
words.ex: The square has two diagonal lines.
words.ex_cn: 这个正方形有两条对角线。
words.en: A diagonal line or movement goes in a sloping direction, for example, from one corner of a square across to the opposite corner.

words.ex: He spoke with clear diction.
words.ex_cn: 他说话吐字清晰。
words.en: Diction refers to the choice and use of words and phrases in speech or writing, or the manner in which words are pronounced.

words.ex: Good digestion helps your body absorb nutrients.
words.ex_cn: 良好的消化有助于身体吸收营养。
words.en: The process by which food is broken down in the stomach and intestines so that the body can absorb it and use it for energy and nutrients.

words.ex: He made a digression to tell a funny story.
words.ex_cn: 他岔开话题讲了个有趣的故事。
words.en: A digression is a temporary departure from the main subject in speech or writing.

words.ex: The doctor used drops to dilate her pupils.
words.ex_cn: 医生用了滴眼液来扩大她的瞳孔。
words.en: If you dilate something such as a part of your body, or if it dilates, it becomes larger or wider.

words.ex: Carbon dioxide makes the air warm.
words.ex_cn: 二氧化碳使空气变暖。
words.en: A compound containing two atoms of oxygen combined with another element or group.

words.ex: He was a faithful disciple of the teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他是老师的一名忠实弟子。
words.en: A disciple is a follower or student of a teacher, leader, or philosopher.

words.ex: The hard chair caused him discomfort.
words.ex_cn: 这把硬椅子让他感到不舒适。
words.en: Discomfort is a feeling of slight pain or physical unease, or a feeling of worry or embarrassment.

words.ex: His discourse on climate change was clear and logical.
words.ex_cn: 他关于气候变化的论述清晰而有逻辑。
words.en: Discourse is spoken or written communication between people, especially serious discussion of a particular subject.

words.tr:
n. 耻辱；丢脸；不光彩
v. 使丢脸；使蒙受耻辱
words.ex: He felt disgrace after lying to his friends.
words.ex_cn: 他向朋友撒谎后感到羞愧。
words.en: If you say that someone is in disgrace, you are emphasizing that other people disapprove of them and do not respect them because of something that they have done.

words.tr:
v. 使不再抱幻想；使理想破灭
n. 幻灭；理想破灭
words.ex: The bad experience disillusioned him about politics.
words.ex_cn: 这次糟糕的经历让他对政治不再抱幻想。
words.en: If a person or thing disillusions you, they make you realize that something is not as good as you thought it was.

words.ex: The old bridge will disintegrate if no one fixes it.
words.ex_cn: 如果没人修理，这座旧桥会瓦解。
words.en: If something disintegrates, it breaks into many small pieces or parts and is destroyed.

words.ex: The judge was disinterested in the case.
words.ex_cn: 法官对这个案件持客观态度。
words.en: If someone is disinterested in something, they have no personal involvement or investment in it and are therefore able to judge it fairly.

words.ex: The sky was dismal and gray all day.
words.ex_cn: 天空一整天都是阴沉灰暗的。
words.en: If you describe something as dismal, you mean that it is very bad or depressing.

words.ex: The horror movie showed a man being dismembered.
words.ex_cn: 那部恐怖电影展示了一名男子被肢解。
words.en: To dismember means to cut, tear, or pull the limbs from a body.

words.ex: The storm disorganized the city's traffic.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴使城市的交通陷入混乱。
words.en: To disorganize something means to disrupt its system or order, making it function less effectively.

words.ex: The nurse will dispense medicine to the patients.
words.ex_cn: 护士将分发药品给病人。
words.en: To dispense means to distribute or provide something, especially in a systematic way, or to prepare and give out medicine.

words.ex: The punishment was disproportionate to the crime.
words.ex_cn: 惩罚与罪行不成比例。
words.en: Something that is disproportionate is surprisingly large or small in comparison to something else.

words.ex: The scandal brought the company into disrepute.
words.ex_cn: 这起丑闻使该公司声名狼藉。
words.en: If someone or something is in disrepute, they have a bad reputation because people think they have done something bad or wrong.

words.ex: The news will disseminate quickly through social media.
words.ex_cn: 这条新闻会通过社交媒体迅速传播。
words.en: To disseminate means to spread or distribute something, especially information, widely.

words.tr: n. 持不同意见者；持异议者
words.ex: He is a dissenter who disagrees with the group.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个与群体意见不同的异议者。
words.en: A dissenter is a person who disagrees with an official or commonly held view.

words.ex: He wrote his dissertation on climate change.
words.ex_cn: 他写了一篇关于气候变化的学位论文。
words.en: A dissertation is a long piece of writing on a particular subject, especially one written for a university degree.

words.tr: adj. 不相似的；不一样的；不同的
words.ex: The two apples are dissimilar in color.
words.ex_cn: 这两个苹果颜色不同。
words.en: If one thing is dissimilar to another, or if two things are dissimilar, they are very different from each other.

words.tr: adj. 令人厌恶的；令人憎恶的；令人不悦的
words.ex: The taste of medicine is distasteful.
words.ex_cn: 药的味道很难吃。
words.en: If something is distasteful to you, you think it is unpleasant, disgusting, or immoral.

words.ex: This painting has a distinctive style.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画有独特的风格。
words.en: Something that is distinctive has a special quality or feature which makes it easily recognizable and different from other things of the same type.

words.tr:
n. 潜水；跳水；暴跌；
v. 潜水；跳水；暴跌；
words.ex: He went for a dive in the sea.
words.ex_cn: 他去海里潜水。
words.en: If you dive into water, you jump in head-first with your arms held straight above your head. Dive is also a noun.

words.tr: adj. 分歧的；发散的；趋异的；
words.ex: The two friends had divergent opinions about the movie.
words.ex_cn: 这两个朋友对这部电影的看法不同。
words.en: If two things diverge, they are different from each other, or they become different from each other.

words.ex: The school values diversity in its students.
words.ex_cn: 学校重视学生的多样性。
words.en: The state of being diverse; variety.

words.tr: v. 缠住；“dog”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The reporter dogged the politician everywhere.
words.ex_cn: 记者紧紧跟随这位政治家到处。
words.en: If you describe someone's actions as dogged, you mean that they are determined to continue with something even if it becomes difficult or dangerous.

words.ex: He refuses to accept the dogma of the church.
words.ex_cn: 他拒绝接受教会的教条。
words.en: A principle or set of principles laid down by an authority as incontrovertibly true.

words.ex: The dolphin jumped high out of the water.
words.ex_cn: 海豚从水中高高跳起。
words.en: A dolphin is a marine mammal that is known for its intelligence and friendly nature towards humans.

words.ex: Humans domesticated dogs thousands of years ago.
words.ex_cn: 人类几千年前就驯养了狗。
words.en: To domesticate an animal or plant means to bring it under human control in order to provide food, power, or company.

words.tr: adj. 休眠的；蛰伏的；暂停活动的
words.ex: The volcano is dormant now.
words.ex_cn: 这座火山现在处于休眠状态。
words.en: Something that is dormant is not active or growing but has the ability to be active at a later time.

words.ex: The dorsal fin helps the fish swim steadily.
words.ex_cn: 背鳍帮助鱼稳定游动。
words.en: Relating to the back or posterior part of an organism or structure.

words.ex: He loves watching drama on TV.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢在电视上看戏剧。
words.en: A drama is a serious play for the theatre, television, or radio, or a serious style of acting intended to represent real life and characters.

words.tr: adj. 沉闷乏味的；忧郁的；凄凉的
words.ex: The weather was dreary and rainy all day.
words.ex_cn: 天气一整天都阴沉沉的，还下着雨。
words.en: If you describe something as dreary, you mean that it is dull, lifeless, or depressing.

words.tr: adj. 昏昏欲睡的；困倦的；催眠的
words.ex: He felt drowsy after lunch.
words.ex_cn: 他午饭后感到昏昏欲睡。
words.en: If you feel drowsy, you feel sleepy and cannot think clearly.

words.tr: n. 单调乏味的苦差事
words.ex: He hates the drudgery of washing dishes every day.
words.ex_cn: 他讨厌每天洗碗的枯燥工作。
words.en: Hard, menial, or dull work.

words.tr: adj. 可延展的；易于塑造的
words.ex: The gold is ductile and can be drawn into thin wires.
words.ex_cn: 金具有延展性，可以拉成细丝。
words.en: A ductile material is one that can be stretched into a wire or hammered into a thin sheet without breaking.

words.ex: The fairy tale features a dwarf who lives in a small house.
words.ex_cn: 这个童话故事中有一个住在小房子里的侏儒。
words.en: A dwarf is a person, animal, or plant that is much smaller than the usual size of its species. As a verb, to dwarf means to make someone or something seem small or insignificant in comparison.

words.ex: The Tang dynasty was famous for its poetry and art.
words.ex_cn: 唐朝以诗歌和艺术而闻名。
words.en: A dynasty is a series of rulers of a country who all belong to the same family.

words.ex: He likes eclecticism in music, from jazz to rock.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢音乐上的折衷主义，从爵士到摇滚。
words.en: Eclecticism is a conceptual approach that does not hold rigidly to a single paradigm or set of assumptions, but instead draws upon multiple theories, styles, or ideas to gain complementary insights into a subject, or applies different theories in particular cases.

words.ex: He tries to economize by walking to work.
words.ex_cn: 他通过步行上班来节省开支。
words.en: To economize means to use less money, time, or resources than usual in order to save them.

words.ex: The old edifice stands near the river.
words.ex_cn: 那座古老的建筑坐落在河边。
words.en: An edifice is a large, impressive building.

words.tr: adj. 受过教育的；有教养的； v. 教育；“educate”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He is an educated man who reads books every day.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个每天都读书的受过教育的人。
words.en: Having been educated; having received education.

words.tr: n. 废水；污物；水流 adj. 流出的
words.ex: The factory releases effluent into the river.
words.ex_cn: 工厂将废水排入河中。
words.en: Effluent is liquid waste material that comes out of factories or sewage works.

words.ex: The election will be held next month.
words.ex_cn: 选举将在下个月举行。
words.en: An election is a process in which people vote to choose a person or group of people to hold an official position.

words.tr: n. 长生不老药；仙丹妙药；
words.ex: The old wizard searched for an elixir to live forever.
words.ex_cn: 这位老巫师寻找一种能让人长生不老的药水。
words.en: An elixir is a magical or medicinal potion, especially one that is supposed to prolong life indefinitely.

words.ex: The track is elliptical in shape.
words.ex_cn: 这个跑道是椭圆形的。
words.en: Something that is elliptical has the shape of an ellipse or is characterized by the omission of words that are understood to be obvious.

words.ex: The artist elongated the figure to create a sense of grace.
words.ex_cn: 艺术家拉长了人物形象，以创造出一种优雅的感觉。
words.en: To elongate something means to make it longer, especially by stretching it.

words.tr: adj. 难以捉摸的；不易被抓获（觉察、理解或记忆）的；
words.ex: The truth remained elusive.
words.ex_cn: 真相难以捉摸。
words.en: Difficult to find, catch, or achieve; difficult to remember or understand.

words.ex: The law will emancipate slaves.
words.ex_cn: 法律将解放奴隶。
words.en: To emancipate someone means to set them free from something that restricts their freedom to do what they want.

words.ex: She embellished the dress with flowers.
words.ex_cn: 她用花朵装饰了这条裙子。
words.en: To embellish something means to make it more attractive by adding decorative details or features.

words.ex: The dove is an emblem of peace.
words.ex_cn: 鸽子是和平的象征。
words.en: An emblem is a design that represents a country, organization, or family.

words.tr: v. 加浮雕花纹于；饰以浮饰；使凸出
words.ex: He embosses the card with his name.
words.ex_cn: 他把名字压印在卡片上。
words.en: To decorate a surface by making raised designs or patterns on it.

words.tr: v. 刺绣；绣（花）；加以渲染（或润色）
words.ex: She embroiders flowers on the pillow.
words.ex_cn: 她在枕头上刺绣花朵。
words.en: To embroider means to decorate cloth or other material by sewing patterns or pictures on it with colored threads.

words.ex: The embryo grows inside the mother's womb.
words.ex_cn: 胚胎在母亲的子宫内生长。
words.en: An embryo is an unborn animal or human being in the very early stages of development.

words.ex: He is an eminent scientist who won the Nobel Prize.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位获得诺贝尔奖的杰出科学家。
words.en: An eminent person is well-known and respected, especially because they are good at their profession.

words.tr:
adj. 空的；无意义的；
v. 倒空；
words.ex: The box is empty.
words.ex_cn: 这个盒子是空的。
words.en: If you describe a place, object, or person as empty, you mean that they contain nothing or have no special qualities, and are therefore not interesting or useful.

words.tr: v. 制定（法律）；通过（法律）；扮演（角色）
words.ex: The government will enact a new law next month.
words.ex_cn: 政府下个月将颁布一项新法律。
words.en: To enact a law or rule means to make it official by passing it through a legislative body.

words.ex: The diamond is encased in glass.
words.ex_cn: 钻石被包裹在玻璃里。
words.en: To encase something means to cover or surround it completely in a case or close-fitting covering.

words.ex: The book encompasses all basic math skills.
words.ex_cn: 这本书包含了所有基础数学技能。
words.en: If something encompasses particular things, it includes them.

words.tr: v. 侵入；侵占；侵犯；侵蚀
words.ex: The new building encroaches on the park.
words.ex_cn: 新建筑侵占了公园。
words.en: To gradually take something such as power or authority from someone else, often in a way that is not fair or legal.

words.ex: The desert seems endless.
words.ex_cn: 这片沙漠看起来无穷无尽。
words.en: If you say that something is endless, you mean that it is very large or lasts for a very long time, and it seems as if it will never stop.

words.tr: v. 从事于；（使）参与；“engage”的现在分词； adj. 有趣的；
words.ex: He is engaging in community service.
words.ex_cn: 他正在从事社区服务。
words.en: An engaging person or thing is pleasant, interesting, and entertaining.

words.ex: He engraves his name on the ring.
words.ex_cn: 他把名字刻在戒指上。
words.en: To engrave means to cut or carve a design or letters into a hard surface, or to be strongly impressed in someone's memory.

words.ex: The unfair rule enrage him.
words.ex_cn: 不公平的规则激怒了他。
words.en: To make someone extremely angry.

words.tr: n. 全体；剧团；合奏曲；套装
words.ex: The ensemble played a beautiful song at the concert.
words.ex_cn: 这个合奏团在音乐会上演奏了一首优美的曲子。
words.en: An ensemble is a group of musicians, actors, or dancers who perform together.

words.ex: The two particles show quantum entanglement.
words.ex_cn: 这两个粒子表现出量子纠缠。
words.en: An entanglement is a complicated or difficult relationship or situation.

words.tr: adj. 有进取心的；有魄力的；
words.ex: He is an enterprising boy who starts small businesses.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个有进取心的男孩，会经营小生意。
words.en: If you describe someone as enterprising, you mean that they are willing to try out new, unusual ways of doing or achieving something.

words.tr: adj. 确立的；根深蒂固的； v. “entrench”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The entrenched system is hard to change.
words.ex_cn: 这个已确立的制度很难改变。
words.en: If something is entrenched, it is firmly established and very difficult to change.

words.ex: He felt envious when his friend got a new bike.
words.ex_cn: 当他的朋友得到一辆新自行车时，他感到嫉妒。
words.en: If you are envious of someone, you want something that they have.

words.ex: He envisions a world without war.
words.ex_cn: 他想象一个没有战争的世界。
words.en: To envision something is to imagine it as a future possibility; it is often used to describe the act of foreseeing or planning for the future.

words.tr: adj. 短暂的；朝生暮死的
words.ex: The flowers are ephemeral and last only one day.
words.ex_cn: 这些花是短暂的，只持续一天。
words.en: Something that is ephemeral lasts for only a very short time.

words.ex: The judge made an equitable decision.
words.ex_cn: 法官做出了一个公平的决定。
words.en: Fair and impartial; treating everyone equally.

words.ex: The government wants to eradicate poverty.
words.ex_cn: 政府希望消灭贫困。
words.en: To eradicate something means to get rid of it completely.

words.tr: adj. 不稳定的；飘忽不定的；
words.ex: The weather has been erratic this month.
words.ex_cn: 这个月的天气一直不稳定。
words.en: Something that is erratic does not follow a regular pattern, but happens at unexpected times or moves in unexpected directions.

words.ex: The argument started small but soon escalate.
words.ex_cn: 争论起初很小，但很快逐步升高。
words.en: If a bad situation escalates or if someone or something escalates it, it becomes greater in size, seriousness, or intensity.

words.ex: He knows good etiquette at dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他知道晚餐时的礼貌规矩。
words.en: Etiquette refers to the customary code of polite behavior in society or among members of a particular profession or group.

words.tr: adj. 充满大事的；多事故的；多变故的
words.ex: It was an eventful day with many surprises.
words.ex_cn: 那是充满惊喜的一天。
words.en: If you describe a period of time as eventful, you mean that a lot of interesting, exciting, or important things have happened during it.

words.tr:
adj. 常绿的；常青的；
n. 常绿树；常绿植物；
words.ex: The evergreen trees stay green all year.
words.ex_cn: 常绿树一年四季都是绿色的。
words.en: An evergreen is a plant, tree, or bush that has green leaves all the year round.

words.tr: v. 取出内脏；重伤元气
words.ex: The cat eviscerated the mouse.
words.ex_cn: 这只猫掏出了老鼠的内脏。
words.en: To eviscerate means to remove the internal organs of a person or animal, or to remove the most important parts of something, leaving it weak or ineffective.

words.tr:
adj. 要求严格的；要求小心仔细的；苛求的
v. 强求；急需；要求；“exact”的现在分词
words.ex: He is an exacting teacher who wants perfect work.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个要求严格的老师，要求完美无缺的作业。
words.en: requiring a lot of effort, care, or attention

words.tr:
adj. 高位的；高尚的；欣喜的
v. 赞扬；提升；加强；“exalt”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: The exalted king sat on a golden throne.
words.ex_cn: 这位高位的国王坐在一张金宝座上。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as exalted, you mean they are at a high level of honor, rank, or quality.

words.ex: Workers excavate the old ruins with shovels.
words.ex_cn: 工人们用铲子挖掘古代遗址。
words.en: To excavate means to dig in the ground in order to find things that have been buried there, such as archaeological remains.

words.tr: adj. 典范的；可做模范的；惩戒性的
words.ex: He is an exemplary student who always finishes his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他是一名模范学生，总是完成作业。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as exemplary, you think they are extremely good and suitable to be copied by other people.

words.ex: He exhale slowly after running.
words.ex_cn: 他跑步后慢慢呼出气。
words.en: To exhale means to breathe out air from your lungs.

words.tr: adj. 筋疲力尽的；耗尽的； v. 耗尽；用完；“exhaust”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He was exhausted after running five kilometers.
words.ex_cn: 他跑完五公里后筋疲力尽。
words.en: If you are exhausted, you are very tired and have no energy left.

words.tr: adj. 令人兴奋的； v. “exhilarate”的现在分词；
words.ex: The roller coaster ride was exhilarating.
words.ex_cn: 过山车之旅令人兴奋。
words.en: If you describe something as exhilarating, you mean that it makes you feel very happy and excited.

words.tr: adj. 过度的；过高的；过分的；
words.ex: The restaurant charged an exorbitant price for a small salad.
words.ex_cn: 这家餐厅对一份小沙拉要了过高的价格。
words.en: If you describe something such as a price or fee as exorbitant, you are emphasizing that it is much higher than it should be.

words.ex: The expanse of the desert stretched far beyond the horizon.
words.ex_cn: 沙漠的辽阔延伸到了地平线之外。
words.en: An expanse is a wide and open area or surface.

words.ex: The population grows exponentially each year.
words.ex_cn: 人口每年呈指数增长。
words.en: Exponential means increasing very rapidly, often used to describe growth rates in mathematics, biology, and economics.

words.ex: Her expressive eyes showed all her feelings.
words.ex_cn: 她富有表情的眼睛展现了她所有的感情。
words.en: If you describe a person or their behaviour as expressive, you mean that their behaviour clearly indicates their feelings or intentions.

words.ex: He expressly told me not to be late.
words.ex_cn: 他特意告诉我不要迟到。
words.en: If something is said or done expressly, it is said or done in a clear, deliberate way.

words.ex: The farmer tried to exterminate the rats.
words.ex_cn: 农夫试图消灭老鼠。
words.en: To exterminate means to kill all the members of a group of people or animals, or to destroy something completely.

words.ex: He extols the beauty of nature every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天赞美大自然的美。
words.en: If you extol something or someone, you praise them enthusiastically.

words.ex: He felt pain in the extremity of his finger.
words.ex_cn: 他手指的末端感到疼痛。
words.en: An extremity is the furthest point or limit of something, or a situation of extreme difficulty or danger.

words.tr: adj. 精力充沛的；热情洋溢的；
words.ex: The exuberant children ran around the park.
words.ex_cn: 那些精力充沛的孩子们在公园里跑来跑去。
words.en: If you are exuberant, you are full of energy, excitement, and cheerfulness.

words.ex: The eyewitness saw the accident happen.
words.ex_cn: 目击者看到了事故的发生。
words.en: An eyewitness is a person who has seen something happen and can give a first-hand description of it.

words.ex: The old building has a beautiful facade with stone pillars.
words.ex_cn: 这栋老建筑有一个带有石柱的漂亮正面。
words.en: The front of a building, especially an imposing or decorative one. Also, a superficial appearance or illusion of something.

words.tr: n. 复制本；摹本；仿制品；传真
words.ex: He sent a facsimile of the document to his office.
words.ex_cn: 他把文件的传真发到了办公室。
words.en: An exact copy of a document, picture, or piece of writing, especially one that has been made by a machine.

words.tr: n. 派系；派系斗争；内讧
words.ex: The faction argued loudly about the new rule.
words.ex_cn: 这个派别就新规定激烈争论。
words.en: A faction is a group of people within a larger group who have different opinions and beliefs from the rest of the group.

words.tr: adj. 根据事实的；真实的；
words.ex: His report is factual and accurate.
words.ex_cn: 他的报告是基于事实且准确的。
words.en: If something is factual, it is based on facts or concerns facts.

words.ex: The falcon flew high above the mountains.
words.ex_cn: 猎鹰在群山上空飞翔。
words.en: A falcon is a bird of prey, known for its speed and keen eyesight, used in falconry.

words.ex: He is fanatical about football.
words.ex_cn: 他对足球非常狂热。
words.en: If you describe someone as fanatical, you mean that they are extremely enthusiastic about a particular activity, subject, or belief, often to an extent that is considered excessive or unreasonable.

words.ex: The trial was a farce.
words.ex_cn: 这场审判是一场闹剧。
words.en: A farce is a comedy that aims at entertaining the audience through situations that are highly exaggerated, extravagant, and thus improbable.

words.tr: adj. 重大的；命中注定的；决定命运的；预言性的
words.ex: It was a fateful day when he met her.
words.ex_cn: 那是他遇见她的命运般的一天。
words.en: If you describe an event or action as fateful, you mean that it has very important and often bad effects on the future.

words.ex: The faucet is dripping.
words.ex_cn: 水龙头在滴水。
words.en: A faucet is a device that controls the flow of a liquid or gas from a pipe or container, especially one that you turn to start or stop the flow of water.

words.tr: n. 过错；故障；缺陷；断层；
words.ex: It was his fault that the car crashed.
words.ex_cn: 汽车撞车是他的过错。
words.en: A fault is a mistake or a weakness in something or someone.

words.ex: Climbing the mountain without oxygen was a great feat.
words.ex_cn: 在不吸氧的情况下爬山是一项伟大的壮举。
words.en: A feat is an act or achievement that shows great courage, skill, or strength.

words.tr:
n. 发酵；酵素；动乱
v. （使）发酵；动乱
words.ex: The ferment of yeast makes bread rise.
words.ex_cn: 酵母的发酵使面包膨胀。
words.en: If a substance ferments or if it is fermented, it changes chemically because of the action of yeast or bacteria, often producing alcohol.

words.ex: He spoke with fervor about his dreams.
words.ex_cn: 他充满热情地谈论自己的梦想。
words.en: Fervor is intense and passionate feeling.

words.ex: The two families have a long feud.
words.ex_cn: 这两个家族有长期的世仇。
words.en: A feud is a prolonged and bitter quarrel or dispute, especially between two families or groups, often involving violence.

words.tr: adj. 发烧的；紧张忙乱的；极度紧张（或兴奋）的
words.ex: He is feverish after running in the sun.
words.ex_cn: 他在太阳下跑步后发高烧。
words.en: If you are feverish, you are suffering from a fever, or you are extremely excited or worried about something.

words.ex: His fidelity to his friend never changed.
words.ex_cn: 他对朋友的忠诚从未改变。
words.en: Fidelity is loyalty to a person, organization, or set of beliefs.

words.tr: n. 装饰船头的人像；傀儡领袖；有名无实的首脑；
words.ex: The old ship had a wooden figurehead of a lion.
words.ex_cn: 那艘旧船的船头有一个木制的狮子像。
words.en: A figurehead is a person who is the head of an organization or country in name only, without any real power or authority.

words.ex: He won the game with great finesse.
words.ex_cn: 他以高超的技巧赢得了比赛。
words.en: If you finesse something, you handle it in a skillful and often slightly deceptive way.

words.ex: The fishy smell came from the old fish in the fridge.
words.ex_cn: 那股鱼腥味来自冰箱里的旧鱼。
words.en: If you describe something as fishy, you mean that it seems suspicious or dishonest.

words.ex: Regular exercise improves your fitness.
words.ex_cn: 规律锻炼能改善你的健康。
words.en: The condition of being physically fit and healthy.

words.ex: He has flabby arms from not exercising.
words.ex_cn: 他因为不锻炼，手臂松软。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as flabby, you are criticizing them for being soft and loose rather than firm and strong.

words.ex: She has a flair for painting.
