words.en: Percussion refers to musical instruments that are played by being struck or shaken, such as drums, cymbals, or tambourines. It can also refer to the act of striking or hitting something.

words.tr: adj. 多年生的；反复出现的；
words.ex: These perennial flowers bloom every year.
words.ex_cn: 这些多年生的花每年都会开花。
words.en: A perennial plant is one that lives for more than two years, often flowering and producing seeds multiple times over its lifespan.

words.ex: The fence marks the perimeter of the garden.
words.ex_cn: 围栏标出了花园的边界。
words.en: The perimeter of an area or object is the total length of its sides or outer boundary.

words.ex: The small village lies on the periphery of the city.
words.ex_cn: 这个小村庄位于城市的外围。
words.en: The outer limits or edge of an area or object.

words.tr:
adj. 垂直的；笔直的
n. 垂直线
words.ex: The lines are perpendicular to each other.
words.ex_cn: 这些线互相垂直。
words.en: At right angles to the plane of the horizon or a base line; vertical.

words.tr: v. 使（尤指不好的情形、体系、信仰）持续、长存；
words.ex: The system perpetuates inequality among the poor.
words.ex_cn: 这个体系使贫困人群的不平等持续存在。
words.en: To perpetuate something means to cause it to continue, especially for a long time.

words.ex: They persecute people for their beliefs.
words.ex_cn: 他们因人们的信仰而迫害他们。
words.en: If someone is persecuted, they are treated cruelly and unfairly, often because of their race, religion, or political beliefs.

words.ex: He persevered despite many failures.
words.ex_cn: 尽管多次失败，他仍然坚持不懈。
words.en: If you persevere with something, you keep trying to do it and do not give up, even though it is difficult.

words.tr: n. 全体人员；人事部；职员；
words.ex: The company hired new personnel last month.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司上个月雇佣了新员工。
words.en: The people who are employed in a company or organization.

words.ex: He wiped away the perspiration from his forehead.
words.ex_cn: 他擦去了额头上的汗。
words.en: Perspiration is the process of sweating, or the sweat itself, that occurs in humans and some animals as a way of regulating body temperature.

words.tr: n. 语文学；语言学；文献学
words.ex: He loves philology because it helps him understand old texts.
words.ex_cn: 他热爱语言学，因为它帮助他理解古文。
words.en: Philology is the study of language in written historical sources; it is a combination of literary studies, history and linguistics.

words.tr:
n. 语音学
adj. 语音的；发音的
words.ex: He is learning phonetics to improve his pronunciation.
words.ex_cn: 他正在学习语音学以改善发音。
words.en: Phonetics is the study of the sounds of human speech.

words.ex: The physician checked the patient's temperature.
words.ex_cn: 医生检查了病人的体温。
words.en: A physician is a medical doctor who is trained in the diagnosis and treatment of diseases and injuries.

words.ex: The village by the lake is picturesque.
words.ex_cn: 湖边的村庄如画般美丽。
words.en: A picturesque place is attractive and interesting, especially in a way that is old-fashioned or unusual.

words.ex: The pigment in leaves changes color in autumn.
words.ex_cn: 叶子中的色素在秋天会变色。
words.en: A pigment is a substance that gives something a particular color.

words.ex: The GPS can pinpoint your exact location.
words.ex_cn: GPS可以精准定位你的准确位置。
words.en: To pinpoint something means to locate or identify it precisely.

words.ex: He was a pioneer in space exploration.
words.ex_cn: 他是太空探索的先驱者。
words.en: A pioneer is someone who is one of the first people to do something that others will later develop or continue. Pioneers are also people who are among the first to go to live in a new area, especially in the past when people were trying to settle in new lands.

words.tr:
v. 激怒；使生气；激起
n. 怨恨；愤恨
words.ex: His rude comment piqued her anger.
words.ex_cn: 他粗鲁的评论激怒了她。
words.en: If something piques your interest or curiosity, it makes you interested or curious.

words.ex: The pirate sailed the sea with a black flag.
words.ex_cn: 海盗带着黑旗在海上航行。
words.en: A pirate is someone who attacks and robs ships at sea. The term can also refer to someone who illegally copies and distributes software, music, or films.

words.tr:
n. 音高；球场；程度（最高点）；宣传论点；
v. 扎营；
words.ex: The singer changed the pitch of her voice.
words.ex_cn: 歌手改变了她声音的音高。
words.en: Pitch can refer to the highness or lowness of a sound, the act of throwing something, or a thick, black, sticky substance used for paving roads or waterproofing.

words.tr:
n. 枢；中心；旋转
v. 在枢轴上转动；以…为中心
words.ex: The door pivots on a hinge.
words.ex_cn: 门围绕一个铰链旋转。
words.en: A pivot is the central point, pin, or shaft on which a mechanism turns or oscillates. It can also refer to the central or most important person or thing in a situation.

words.ex: He was punished for plagiarism in his essay.
words.ex_cn: 他因论文剽窃而受到惩罚。
words.en: Plagiarism is the practice of using or copying someone else's idea or work and pretending that you thought of it or created it.

words.tr:
n. 平原；
adj. 简单明了的；朴素的；
words.ex: The cows graze on the plain.
words.ex_cn: 牛在平原上吃草。
words.en: If something is plain, it is easy to see, hear, or understand.

words.ex: He nailed the wooden plank to the floor.
words.ex_cn: 他把木板钉在了地板上。
words.en: A plank is a long, flat piece of wood, often used in building or as part of a structure.

words.ex: The farmer worked on the plantation every day.
words.ex_cn: 农夫每天在耕地上劳作。
words.en: A plantation is a large piece of land, especially in a tropical country, where crops such as coffee, sugar, rubber, or tobacco are grown.

words.tr: n. 陈词滥调；老生常谈；
words.ex: His speech was full of platitudes about hard work.
words.ex_cn: 他的演讲充满了关于努力工作的陈词滥调。
words.en: A platitude is a statement that has been used so often that it is meaningless and shows a lack of original thought.

words.ex: He is a famous playwright who writes plays.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位著名的剧作家，写剧本。
words.en: A playwright is a person who writes plays.

words.tr: adj. 令人高兴的； v. “please”的现在分词；
words.ex: The pleasing smell of cookies made her smile.
words.ex_cn: 饼干令人高兴的香味让她笑了。
words.en: Something that is pleasing gives you pleasure or satisfaction.

words.ex: The plastic is pliable and easy to bend.
words.ex_cn: 这种塑料柔韧，容易弯曲。
words.en: A pliable object or material is easy to bend or shape without breaking.

words.ex: The family is in a difficult plight after losing their home.
words.ex_cn: 这家人在失去家园后陷入了困境。
words.en: A plight is a difficult or adverse situation, especially one that is hard to escape. It can also refer to a solemn promise or pledge.

words.tr:
n. 犁；犁形器具
v. 犁；耕；艰苦前进
words.ex: The farmer uses a plow to turn the soil.
words.ex_cn: 农夫用犁翻土。
words.en: A plow is a farm tool with one or more heavy blades that breaks the soil and cuts a furrow for sowing seeds.

words.ex: The bird's plumage was a vibrant mix of colors.
words.ex_cn: 这只鸟的羽毛色彩鲜艳。
words.en: The feathers covering the body of a bird.

words.ex: The builder used a plumb to check if the wall was straight.
words.ex_cn: 建筑工人用铅锤检查墙是否垂直。
words.en: To measure the depth of water with a plumb line; to explore or understand something deeply; exactly vertical; completely or directly.

words.tr:
adj. 丰满的；肥胖的
v. （使）圆胖；（使）鼓起
adv. 噗通地；直接地
words.ex: The baby has plump cheeks.
words.ex_cn: 这个婴儿有圆润的脸颊。
words.en: Having a full rounded shape; chubby.

words.ex: He got pneumonia after a bad cold.
words.ex_cn: 他得了重感冒后患了肺炎。
words.en: Pneumonia is a serious disease which affects your lungs and makes it difficult for you to breathe.

words.tr: n. 小笔记本；钱夹；袖珍本；财力
words.ex: He wrote the phone number in his pocketbook.
words.ex_cn: 他把电话号码写在了他的小笔记本里。
words.en: A pocketbook is a small book, especially one that can be carried in a pocket, or a woman's handbag.

words.ex: He is interested in politics.
words.ex_cn: 他对政治感兴趣。
words.en: Politics are the actions or activities concerned with achieving and using power in a country or society. The verb that follows politics may be either singular or plural.

words.ex: Bees pollinate flowers in the garden.
words.ex_cn: 蜜蜂给花园里的花授粉。
words.en: To pollinate means to transfer pollen from the male part of a flower to the female part, enabling fertilization and the production of seeds.

words.ex: The factory pollutes the river.
words.ex_cn: 工厂污染了这条河。
words.en: To pollute water, air, or land means to make it dirty and dangerous to live in or to use, especially with poisonous chemicals or waste.

words.ex: He drew a pentagon, which is a polygon.
words.ex_cn: 他画了一个五边形，它是一个多边形。
words.en: A polygon is a flat shape with three or more straight sides and angles.

words.tr: adj. 沉重的；笨重的；沉闷的
words.ex: He carried a ponderous box across the room.
words.ex_cn: 他搬着一个沉重的箱子穿过房间。
words.en: Something that is ponderous is very heavy or is very slow and clumsy because of its weight or size.

words.tr: adj. 人口众多的；人口密集的
words.ex: China is a populous country.
words.ex_cn: 中国是一个人口众多的国家。
words.en: If a place is populous, it has a large population.

words.ex: He bought a porcelain cup at the market.
words.ex_cn: 他在市场上买了一个瓷杯。
words.en: A hard, white, translucent ceramic that is made by firing a pure clay and then glazing it.

words.ex: Dark clouds portend a storm.
words.ex_cn: 乌云预示着一场风暴。
words.en: If something portends something else, it indicates that it is likely to happen in the future.

words.tr: adj. 死后的；死后出版的；遗腹的
words.ex: He received a posthumous award for his bravery.
words.ex_cn: 他因勇敢而被追授了奖项。
words.en: Posthumous means occurring, awarded, or appearing after the death of the originator.

words.ex: She poured tea from the pot.
words.ex_cn: 她从壶里倒出了茶。
words.en: A pot is a deep round container used for cooking.

words.ex: The medicine is potent and works quickly.
words.ex_cn: 这种药物非常有效，起效很快。
words.en: Something that is potent is very effective and powerful.

words.ex: He buys poultry at the local market.
words.ex_cn: 他在当地市场买家禽。
words.en: Poultry refers to domesticated birds kept by humans for their eggs, meat, or feathers.

words.ex: The book costs five pounds.
words.ex_cn: 这本书五英镑。
words.en: The pound is the unit of money used in Britain. It is also a unit of weight equal to 16 ounces or 0.4536 kilograms. As a verb, to pound means to hit something hard many times or to crush something into a powder or paste.

words.ex: The cows graze on the prairie.
words.ex_cn: 牛在草原上吃草。
words.en: A prairie is a large area of flat, grassy land, especially in North America.

words.tr: adj. 不安全的；危险的；不稳当的；
words.ex: The ladder was precarious and might fall.
words.ex_cn: 梯子不安全，可能会倒。
words.en: If a situation is precarious, it is uncertain or dangerous, and could get worse or fail.

words.ex: The bicycle was a precursor to the car.
words.ex_cn: 自行车是汽车的先驱。
words.en: A precursor is something that happened or existed before another thing, especially if it either developed into it or had an influence on it.

words.ex: The lion is a predatory animal.
words.ex_cn: 狮子是一种食肉动物。
words.en: Predatory animals live by killing and eating other animals. Predatory people or organizations are eager to gain something out of someone else's weakness or suffering.

words.ex: The city is predominantly populated by young people.
words.ex_cn: 这个城市主要由年轻人居住。
words.en: If something is predominantly true, it is true to a much greater extent than it is false.

words.tr: v. 占主导地位；占支配地位；
words.ex: English predominate in this region.
words.ex_cn: 英语在这个地区占主导地位。
words.en: If one type of person or thing predominates in a group, there is more of that type than of any other.

words.tr: adj. 杰出的；卓越的；出类拔萃的
words.ex: He is a pre-eminent scientist in his field.
words.ex_cn: 他是该领域最杰出的科学家。
words.en: If someone or something is pre-eminent in a group, they are more important, powerful, or capable than other people or things in the group.

words.tr: adj. 预制的； v. “prefabricate”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The house was built with prefabricated parts.
words.ex_cn: 这所房子是由预制构件建造的。
words.en: Prefabricated buildings or objects are built from parts that have been made in a factory and can be put together quickly.

words.tr: adj. 较合意的；更可取的；
words.ex: Tea is preferable to coffee in the morning.
words.ex_cn: 早上喝茶比喝咖啡更合意。
words.en: If you say that one thing is preferable to another, you mean that it is more desirable or suitable.

words.ex: The cave paintings are prehistoric.
words.ex_cn: 这些洞穴壁画是史前的。
words.en: Belonging to or existing in times before recorded history.

words.ex: His preoccupation with video games made him ignore his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他对电子游戏的全神贯注让他忽略了作业。
words.en: If you have a preoccupation with something or someone, you think or worry about them very often and they are the main focus of your attention.

words.ex: The preponderance of evidence shows he is guilty.
words.ex_cn: 大多数证据表明他有罪。
words.en: If there is a preponderance of one type of thing or person in a group, there are more of that type than of any other.

words.ex: You need basic math as a prerequisite for this course.
words.ex_cn: 你学习这门课程的前提是掌握基础数学。
words.en: A prerequisite is something that must exist or happen before something else can exist or happen.

words.tr: n. 总统职位；总统任期
words.ex: He won the presidency in 2020.
words.ex_cn: 他在2020年赢得了总统职位。
words.en: The position or term of office of a president.

words.tr: n. 自命不凡；自称；标榜；虚荣
words.ex: His pretension made others think he was better than them.
words.ex_cn: 他的自命不凡让别人觉得他比他们强。
words.en: If you say that someone has pretensions, you mean that they claim or pretend that they are more important, intelligent, or skilled than they really are.

words.tr: adj. 盛行的；有优势的；普遍的； v. “prevail”的现在分词；
words.ex: The prevailing weather today is sunny.
words.ex_cn: 今天盛行的天气是晴天。
words.en: The prevailing thing in a particular place or at a particular time is the one that is most common or strongest at that place or time.

words.ex: The primal forest has never been touched by humans.
words.ex_cn: 这片原始森林从未被人类触碰过。
words.en: Primal means relating to an early stage in the development of something, or being the most important or basic part of something.

words.ex: Monkeys and apes are primates.
words.ex_cn: 猴子和猿类是灵长类动物。
words.en: A primate is a member of the most developed and intelligent group of mammals, which includes humans, apes, and monkeys. In a religious context, a primate can also refer to the chief bishop or archbishop in a province or country.

words.tr: adj. 原始的；远古的；最初的
words.ex: The primordial soup formed the first life on Earth.
words.ex_cn: 原始汤形成了地球上的最初生命。
words.en: Primordial means existing at or from the beginning of time; primeval.

words.ex: The forest remained pristine and untouched.
words.ex_cn: 这片森林保持原始且未被破坏。
words.en: Something that is pristine is in its original condition and has not been spoiled or damaged.

words.tr:
v. 戳；刺；激励；督促
n. 戳；刺；催促
words.ex: He prodded the fire with a stick.
words.ex_cn: 他用一根棍子戳了戳火。
words.en: To poke or jab someone or something, often with a finger or a pointed object, in order to get their attention or to encourage them to do something.

words.tr: adj. 惊人的；巨大的；奇异的；巨大的；
words.ex: He showed a prodigious memory for names.
words.ex_cn: 他对名字有着惊人的记忆力。
words.en: If you describe something as prodigious, you are emphasizing that it is very large or impressive.

words.ex: This school uses a progressive teaching method.
words.ex_cn: 这所学校使用一种先进的教学方法。
words.en: A progressive person or idea is one that is modern and new, and is interested in change and improvement.

words.ex: Rabbits proliferate quickly in the wild.
words.ex_cn: 兔子在野外繁殖得很快。
words.en: If something proliferates, it increases in number or spreads quickly.

words.ex: He is a prolific writer who publishes books every year.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位多产的作家，每年都会出版书籍。
words.en: A prolific artist, writer, or composer produces a large number of works of art, books, or pieces of music.

words.tr: v. 发音；宣告；“pronounce”的过去式和过去分词； adj. 显著的；
words.ex: He pronounced the word correctly.
words.ex_cn: 他正确地发音了这个单词。
words.en: Something that is pronounced is very noticeable or obvious.

words.ex: He has a propensity for telling the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他有说实话的倾向。
words.en: A propensity is a natural tendency to behave in a particular way.

words.tr: n. 支持者；拥护者；辩护者
words.ex: He is a proponent of clean energy.
words.ex_cn: 他是清洁能源的支持者。
words.en: A proponent of an idea or course of action is someone who supports it and tries to persuade other people to support it.

words.tr: n. 所有者；经营者 ；业主
words.ex: The proprietor runs a small coffee shop.
words.ex_cn: 店主经营一家小咖啡馆。
words.en: A proprietor is a person who owns a particular type of business, especially a hotel, a shop, or a company.

words.ex: The rocket uses chemical propulsion to fly into space.
words.ex_cn: 火箭使用化学推进力飞入太空。
words.en: Propulsion is the force that moves something forward, especially in vehicles like cars, planes, or spacecraft.

words.ex: The court will prosecute him for theft.
words.ex_cn: 法院将因盗窃罪起诉他。
words.en: To prosecute means to institute legal proceedings against someone or to carry on a legal action against a defendant in a court of law. It also means to continue with or carry on an activity or enterprise.

words.ex: He is the protagonist in the story.
words.ex_cn: 他是故事中的主角。
words.en: The main character in a story, play, film, etc., especially the one who is good or who the audience is expected to support.

words.tr: adj. 谨慎的；慎重的；精明的
words.ex: He is prudent with his money.
words.ex_cn: 他在花钱时很谨慎。
words.en: If you are prudent, you are careful and avoid taking unnecessary risks.

words.ex: He wants to publicize his new book.
words.ex_cn: 他想宣传他的新书。
words.en: To publicize something means to make it widely known to the public, especially by using the media.

words.ex: The dog stepped in a puddle.
words.ex_cn: 狗踩进了一个水坑。
words.en: A puddle is a small pool of liquid, especially of rainwater on the ground.

words.ex: The pueblo is old and has stone houses.
words.ex_cn: 这个普韦布洛很古老，有石屋。
words.en: A pueblo is a type of Indian village built by certain peoples in the south-western United States, especially one consisting of multistorey adobe houses built by the Pueblo people.

words.ex: The orange was squeezed into a sweet pulp.
words.ex_cn: 橙子被榨成了甜美的浆状物。
words.en: The soft, wet, shapeless mass of material that is left after the juice has been removed from fruit or vegetables, or the soft inner part of a tooth.

words.ex: The doctor checked his pulse with his fingers.
words.ex_cn: 医生用手指检查了他的脉搏。
words.en: A pulse is the regular beating of the heart, especially when it is felt at the wrist or neck. It can also refer to a single vibration or short burst of sound, electric current, light, etc.

words.ex: He punched the wall in anger.
words.ex_cn: 他生气地打了墙一拳。
words.en: To punch means to hit someone or something hard with your fist, or to make a hole in something using a tool.

words.tr:
n. 刺穿；刺孔
v. 刺穿；削弱
words.ex: The bike tire has a puncture.
words.ex_cn: 自行车轮胎有一个漏气孔。
words.en: A puncture is a small hole made by a sharp object, especially in a tire. To puncture something means to make a hole in it with a sharp object.

words.tr: adj. 刺鼻的；一语道破的
words.ex: The cheese has a pungent smell.
words.ex_cn: 这种奶酪有刺鼻的气味。
words.en: Having a sharply strong taste or smell.

words.tr:
n. 鹌鹑；鹌鹑肉 
v. 畏缩；胆怯
words.ex: The farmer raised quail for their eggs.
words.ex_cn: 农夫饲养鹌鹑来获取它们的蛋。
words.en: If someone quails, they feel or show fear or hesitation.

words.ex: The village has a quaint old church.
words.ex_cn: 这个村庄有一座古色古香的古老教堂。
words.en: Something that is quaint is attractive because it is unusual and old-fashioned.

words.ex: The workers load stones from the quarry.
words.ex_cn: 工人们从采石场装载石头。
words.en: A quarry is a place where stone, sand, etc., is dug out of the ground. It can also refer to an animal or person that is being hunted or chased.

words.ex: The volcano is quiescent now.
words.ex_cn: 这座火山现在处于休眠状态。
words.en: Someone or something that is quiescent is quiet and inactive.

words.ex: She makes a quilt for her baby.
words.ex_cn: 她为宝宝做了一床被子。
words.en: A quilt is a bed cover made by sewing layers of fabric together, often with a layer of padding in between, to provide warmth.

words.ex: The factory has a quota of 1000 units per day.
words.ex_cn: 这家工厂每天有1000件的配额。
words.en: A quota is the limited number or quantity of something which is officially allowed.

words.ex: They crossed the river on a wooden raft.
words.ex_cn: 他们乘着木筏渡过了河。
words.en: A raft is a flat structure made of pieces of wood tied together, which is used as a boat or floating platform.

words.ex: He wore a ragged coat in winter.
words.ex_cn: 他冬天穿着一件破旧的外套。
words.en: Clothes that are ragged are old and torn.

words.ex: He plays ragtime on the piano.
words.ex_cn: 他弹奏拉格泰姆音乐。
words.en: Ragtime is a type of music that was popular in the early 20th century, characterized by a syncopated melodic line and regularly accented accompaniment.

words.ex: Last month's rainfall was very low.
words.ex_cn: 上个月的降雨量非常少。
words.en: Rainfall is the amount of rain that falls in a particular area during a particular period.

words.tr: adj. 泛滥的；猖獗的；蔓生的
words.ex: Rumors are rampant in the small town.
words.ex_cn: 谣言在这个小镇上四处流传。
words.en: If you describe something bad, such as a crime or disease, as rampant, you mean that it is very common and is increasing in an uncontrolled way.

words.tr: n. 大牧场主；大牧场工人
words.ex: The rancher feeds his cows every morning.
words.ex_cn: 牧民每天早上喂他的牛。
words.en: A rancher is someone who owns or manages a large farm, especially one used for raising cattle or sheep.

words.ex: The Senate will ratify the treaty next week.
words.ex_cn: 参议院下周将批准这项条约。
words.en: If a country or organization ratifies a treaty or agreement, they make it official by giving their formal approval to it, usually by signing it or voting for it.

words.tr:
n. 定量；配给量
v. 配给；定量供应
words.ex: He gets a small ration of food each day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天得到少量的食物配给。
words.en: A ration is a fixed amount of something such as food or fuel that is officially allowed to each person, especially when there is not enough of it available.

words.tr:
n. 拨浪鼓；嘎嘎声；咔嗒声
v. 发出格格声；使紧张不安；喋喋不休
words.ex: The baby laughed while shaking the rattle.
words.ex_cn: 宝宝摇着拨浪鼓笑了。
words.en: If something rattles or if you rattle it, it makes short sharp knocking sounds as it moves or shakes.

words.tr: adj. 沙哑的；粗声的；喧闹的
words.ex: His raucous voice made it hard to understand him.
words.ex_cn: 他沙哑的声音让他很难被听清楚。
words.en: A raucous sound is loud and harsh.

words.ex: The river flows through a deep ravine.
words.ex_cn: 河流流经一个深谷。
words.en: A ravine is a deep, narrow gorge with steep sides, often carved by a river or stream.

words.tr: v. 使夷为平地；彻底摧毁
words.ex: They will raze the old building next week.
words.ex_cn: 他们下周将把那座旧建筑夷为平地。
words.en: To raze a building, town, or forest means to completely destroy it, especially by knocking it down or burning it.

words.ex: He uses a razor to shave every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上用剃须刀刮胡子。
words.en: A razor is a tool with a sharp blade or set of blades, used to remove hair from the face or body.

words.tr:
v. 指责；斥责
n. 指责；谴责
words.ex: The teacher gave him a rebuke for talking in class.
words.ex_cn: 老师因为他上课讲话而责备了他。
words.en: If you rebuke someone, you speak severely to them because they have said or done something that you do not approve of.

words.ex: The trash receptacle is full.
words.ex_cn: 垃圾桶满了。
words.en: A receptacle is an object or space used to contain something.

words.tr: adj. 善于接受的；能接纳的；
words.ex: He is receptive to new ideas.
words.ex_cn: 他善于接受新想法。
words.en: Willing to consider or accept new suggestions and ideas.

words.ex: He recoiled when he saw the snake.
words.ex_cn: 当他看到蛇时，他退缩了。
words.en: If something makes you recoil, you move your body quickly away from it because it frightens, offends, or hurts you.

words.ex: He smiled at the recollection of his childhood.
words.ex_cn: 他回忆起童年时微笑了。
words.en: The act of remembering something or the ability to remember.

words.ex: They will reconstruct the old bridge next year.
words.ex_cn: 他们明年将重建这座旧桥。
words.en: If you reconstruct something that has been destroyed or badly damaged, you build it and make it work again.

words.tr:
v. 细述；叙述
n. 叙述；重新计票
words.ex: He tried to recount the accident to the police.
words.ex_cn: 他试图向警察重新叙述那场事故。
words.en: To recount means to tell someone about something that happened, often in detail; or to count something again to make sure the number is correct.

words.ex: He wound the fishing line onto the reel.
words.ex_cn: 他把鱼线绕在卷筒上。
words.en: A reel is a cylinder on which film, wire, thread, or other flexible materials can be wound. It can also refer to a lively Scottish or Irish dance, or to the act of staggering or lurching violently.

words.ex: The refraction of light makes the straw look bent in water.
words.ex_cn: 光的折光使水中的吸管看起来弯曲了。
words.en: The change in direction of a wave, such as light or sound, when it passes from one medium into another of different density.

words.ex: Please refrigerate the milk after opening.
words.ex_cn: 打开牛奶后请冷藏。
words.en: To refrigerate something means to make it cold, usually in a refrigerator, in order to preserve it.

words.tr: v. 重新刷新；翻新；整修
words.ex: They will refurbish the old house next month.
words.ex_cn: 他们下个月将翻新这栋老房子。
words.en: To refurbish something means to clean it, decorate it, and provide it with new equipment or facilities, especially so that it is more attractive or more useful.

words.ex: The forest shows regeneration after the fire.
words.ex_cn: 森林在火灾后显示出再生。
words.en: The process of renewal, restoration, and growth that makes cells, organisms, and ecosystems resilient to natural fluctuations or events that cause disturbance or damage.

words.tr: v. 恢复；修复；改造（罪犯）
words.ex: The hospital will rehabilitate the injured athlete.
words.ex_cn: 医院将帮助受伤的运动员康复。
words.en: To rehabilitate someone who has been ill or in prison means to help them to live a normal life again. To rehabilitate a building or an area means to improve its condition.

words.ex: The actors rehearse their lines every evening.
words.ex_cn: 演员们每天晚上排练他们的台词。
words.en: To rehearse means to practice a play, piece of music, or other work for later public performance.

words.ex: The company will reimburse you for your travel expenses.
words.ex_cn: 公司会报销你的旅行费用。
words.en: If you reimburse someone for something, you pay them back the money that they have spent or lost because of it.

words.tr: v. 反复地说；重申；重述
words.ex: He reiterate that he is sorry.
words.ex_cn: 他反复地说他很抱歉。
words.en: If you reiterate something, you say it again, usually in order to emphasize it.

words.tr: v. 使年轻； 使恢复精神； 使复原
words.ex: The new sleep routine helps rejuvenate her energy.
words.ex_cn: 新的睡眠习惯帮助她恢复精力。
words.en: To rejuvenate someone or something means to make them look or feel young, fresh, or lively again.

words.ex: He wrote her a letter to rekindle their friendship.
words.ex_cn: 他给她写了一封信，想重新激起他们的友谊。
words.en: To rekindle something means to make it start again or become active again after it has stopped or become less active.

words.ex: The rendition of the song by the singer moved everyone.
words.ex_cn: 歌手对这首歌的演出打动了所有人。
words.en: A rendition of a play, poem, or piece of music is a performance of it.

words.tr: v. 声明放弃；与...断绝关系
words.ex: He renounced his citizenship last year.
words.ex_cn: 他去年放弃了国籍。
words.en: If you renounce a belief or a way of behaving, you say and show that you no longer hold that belief or will behave in that way.

words.ex: He repents for lying to his mother.
words.ex_cn: 他为对母亲撒谎而悔恨。
words.en: If you repent, you feel or express sincere regret or remorse about something wrong you have done.

words.ex: The theater's repertory includes classic plays and modern dramas.
words.ex_cn: 这家剧院的全部剧目包括经典戏剧和现代戏剧。
words.en: A repertory is a collection of pieces of music or plays that a company or performer knows or is prepared to perform.

words.ex: She replenished the water bottle after the hike.
words.ex_cn: 她在徒步后补充了水瓶里的水。
words.en: If you replenish something, you make it full or complete again.

words.ex: He bought a replica of the ancient statue.
words.ex_cn: 他买了一件古代雕像的复制品。
words.en: A replica of something such as a statue, building, or weapon is an accurate copy of it.

words.ex: He tried to repress his anger.
words.ex_cn: 他试图抑制自己的愤怒。
words.en: If you repress a feeling, you deliberately do not express it, often because it is considered unacceptable or inappropriate.

words.tr:
v. 击退；回绝；憎恶
n. 拒斥；击退；严拒
words.ex: The soldiers repulse the enemy attack.
words.ex_cn: 士兵们击退了敌人的进攻。
words.en: If you repulse someone, you reject them or make them feel disgusted.

words.tr:
adj. 据说的；号称的；有名气的
v. 认为；以为；“repute”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: He is a reputed doctor in this city.
words.ex_cn: 他是这座城市里有名的医生。
words.en: Generally believed to be a particular thing, although this might not be true.

words.ex: The residue left in the cup was sugar.
words.ex_cn: 杯子里留下的残留物是糖。
words.en: A residue of something is a small amount that remains after the main part has gone or been taken or used.

words.tr: adj. 坚决的；毅然的；有决心的；
words.ex: He was resolute in his decision to quit smoking.
words.ex_cn: 他决心戒烟。
words.en: If you describe someone as resolute, you approve of them because they are very determined not to change their mind or not to give up a course of action.

words.ex: Breathing deeply helps with respiration.
words.ex_cn: 深呼吸有助于呼吸。
words.en: The process of breathing, which involves inhaling oxygen and exhaling carbon dioxide.

words.tr: adj. 易反应的；应答的；回答的；
words.ex: The child is responsive to his mother's voice.
words.ex_cn: 这个孩子对母亲的声音反应灵敏。
words.en: If someone or something is responsive, they react quickly and favorably.

words.tr: v. 将机械重新整备；重组
words.ex: The factory had to retool to meet new production standards.
words.ex_cn: 工厂必须更换工具以满足新的生产标准。
words.en: To retool means to alter or adapt something, especially machinery or a system, so that it can be used for a different purpose or in a different way.

words.ex: He tried to retract his words after the argument.
words.ex_cn: 他在争吵后试图收回他的话。
words.en: If you retract something that you have said or written, you say that you did not mean it.

words.ex: They revere their grandfather for his wisdom.
words.ex_cn: 他们因祖父的智慧而尊敬他。
words.en: If you revere someone or something, you respect and admire them greatly.

words.tr: n. 新生；振兴；恢复元气
words.ex: The city plan aims at revitalization of old parks.
words.ex_cn: 这个城市计划旨在使旧公园重新焕发生机。
words.en: The process of making something grow, develop, or become successful again.

words.tr: n. 修辞学；花言巧语；华丽的文辞；
words.ex: He studied rhetoric to improve his speaking skills.
words.ex_cn: 他学习修辞学以提高自己的演讲能力。
words.en: Rhetoric is the art or study of using language effectively and persuasively.

words.tr:
n. 谜语；费解的事
v. 解谜；出谜；使布满窟窿；打洞
words.ex: He told me a riddle and I solved it.
words.ex_cn: 他给我出了一道谜语，我解出来了。
words.en: A riddle is a question or statement that is deliberately very confusing and has a clever or amusing answer.

words.ex: There is a small rift in the wall.
words.ex_cn: 墙上有一条小裂缝。
words.en: A rift is a major fault or break in the Earth's crust.

words.tr: n. 坚硬；严格；刚直；死板
words.ex: The rigidity of the metal made it hard to bend.
words.ex_cn: 金属的刚性使其难以弯曲。
words.en: The quality or state of being rigid; stiffness; inflexibility.

words.ex: Rinse the dishes with water before drying them.
words.ex_cn: 在晾干盘子之前用清水冲洗。
words.en: To rinse something means to wash it in clean water in order to remove soap or dirt.

words.ex: It's risky to walk alone at night.
words.ex_cn: 晚上独自走路是危险的。
words.en: If an activity or action is risky, it is dangerous or likely to fail.

words.ex: He writes a letter every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天写一封信。
words.en: To write means to form letters, words, or symbols on a surface in order to communicate.

words.ex: The rivalry between the two teams is very strong.
words.ex_cn: 这两支队伍之间的竞争非常激烈。
words.en: Competition for the same objective or for superiority in the same field.

words.ex: The cat likes to roam around the garden.
words.ex_cn: 这只猫喜欢在花园里游荡。
words.en: To roam means to move about or travel without any definite purpose or destination.

words.ex: The chickens roost on the branch at night.
words.ex_cn: 鸡晚上栖息在树枝上。
words.en: A roost is a place where birds rest or sleep. As a verb, to roost means for birds to settle or rest, typically for the night.

words.ex: There are roughly 100 students in the class.
words.ex_cn: 这个班级大约有100名学生。
words.en: In a manner that is not exact or detailed; approximately.

words.ex: The car turned at the roundabout near the park.
words.ex_cn: 汽车在公园附近的环形交叉路口转弯。
words.en: A roundabout is a circular area at a place where several roads meet. You drive round it until you come to the road that you want.

words.tr: adj. 似橡胶的；有弹性的；软弱无力的
words.ex: The candy has a rubbery texture.
words.ex_cn: 这种糖果有橡皮般的质地。
words.en: Resembling rubber in texture or flexibility; elastic.

words.ex: The children played on the rubble after the building fell.
words.ex_cn: 建筑物倒塌后，孩子们在碎石上玩耍。
words.en: Rubble is the broken pieces of stone, brick, etc., that are left when a building falls down or is destroyed.

words.tr: adj. 未充分发展的；初步的；基本的；
words.ex: His knowledge of math is rudimentary.
words.ex_cn: 他对数学的了解是初步的。
words.en: Rudimentary means relating to the basic or simplest aspects of a subject, or being in the earliest stages of development.

words.ex: The hikers walked on a rugged trail.
words.ex_cn: 徒步者走在一条崎岖的小路上。
words.en: A rugged area of land is uneven and covered with rocks, with few trees or plants.

words.tr:
n. 隆隆声；辘辘声
v. 隆隆作响；辘辘行驶
words.ex: The dog let out a low rumble.
words.ex_cn: 狗发出了一声低沉的咆哮。
words.en: To make a continuous deep, resonant sound; to speak in a low, deep voice.

words.tr:
adj. 乡村的；纯朴的；土气的
n. 乡下人；乡巴佬
words.ex: They live in a rustic cabin near the woods.
words.ex_cn: 他们住在森林附近的一间乡村小屋里。
words.en: Rustic is used to describe things that are typical of the countryside rather than the town, or things that are simple and old-fashioned in a way that is considered typical of the countryside.

words.tr: adj. 无情的；冷酷的；残忍的；
words.ex: The ruthless boss fired employees without warning.
words.ex_cn: 这位无情的老板未经警告就解雇了员工。
words.en: If you say that someone is ruthless, you mean that you disapprove of them because they are very harsh or cruel, and will do anything that is necessary to achieve what they want.

words.ex: He told a long saga about his grandfather's adventures.
words.ex_cn: 他讲了一个关于他祖父冒险的漫长故事。
words.en: A long, detailed story of connected events, especially one that is passed from one generation to the next.

words.ex: He did it for her sake.
words.ex_cn: 他为了她的缘故做了这件事。
words.en: If you do something for the sake of something, you do it for that purpose or in order to achieve that result. You can also say that you do it for something's sake.

words.ex: The salient point in the report is the cost increase.
words.ex_cn: 报告中最显著的要点是成本上升。
words.en: The most noticeable or important.

words.ex: The wound was cleaned with saline water.
words.ex_cn: 伤口用盐水清洗。
words.en: Saline is used to describe something that contains salt or is related to salt.

words.tr:
n. 敬礼；致敬；行礼
v. 敬礼；致敬；行礼
words.ex: The soldier gave a salute to the officer.
words.ex_cn: 士兵向军官敬礼。
words.en: If you salute someone, you greet them or show your respect with a formal sign. Soldiers usually salute officers by raising their right hand so that their fingers touch their forehead.

words.tr: adj. 装作圣洁的；伪善的
words.ex: He gave a sanctimonious speech about honesty.
words.ex_cn: 他做了一番关于诚实的伪善演讲。
words.en: If you describe someone as sanctimonious, you disapprove of them because you think that they are trying to appear morally better than other people.

words.tr: n. 避难所；庇护所；庇护；
words.ex: The birds found sanctuary in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 这些鸟在森林里找到了避难所。
words.en: A sanctuary is a place where people or animals are protected from danger or trouble.

words.ex: The beach has sandy soil.
words.ex_cn: 这个海滩有含沙的土壤。
words.en: Covered with or consisting mostly of sand.

words.tr: n. 公共卫生；卫生设施；
words.ex: The city improved sanitation to keep people healthy.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市改善了公共卫生以保障人民健康。
words.en: The conditions and processes that help maintain health and prevent disease, especially through cleanliness.

words.tr:
n. 树液；
v. 使逐渐耗竭；使削弱；
words.ex: The tree releases sap in spring.
words.ex_cn: 这棵树在春天流出树液。
words.en: Sap is the watery fluid that circulates in the vascular system of a plant, carrying nutrients and sugars. It can also refer to the vitality or energy of a person or thing.

words.tr: adj. 讽刺的；嘲讽的；挖苦的
words.ex: He gave a sarcastic laugh when she said she was perfect.
words.ex_cn: 当她说自己完美时，他讽刺地笑了一声。
words.en: If you describe someone as sarcastic, you mean that they are inclined to say things which are the opposite of what they really mean, especially in order to mock or insult someone.

words.ex: The movie is a satire about politicians.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影是一部关于政治家的讽刺作品。
words.en: A way of criticizing people or ideas in a humorous way, especially in order to make a political point, or a piece of writing that uses this style.

words.tr:
n. 替罪羊；代人受过者
v. 使…成为替罪羊
words.ex: He was made the scapegoat for the company's financial failures.
words.ex_cn: 他被当作公司财务失败的替罪羊。
words.en: A scapegoat is a person who is blamed for something that someone else has done.

words.tr: adj. 深红的；绯红的；猩红的；
words.ex: The scarlet leaves fell in autumn.
words.ex_cn: 深红色的叶子在秋天飘落。
words.en: A brilliant red color.

words.ex: The dog is a scavenger and eats leftover food.
words.ex_cn: 这只狗是拾荒者，吃剩下的食物。
words.en: A scavenger is an animal that feeds on dead organisms, especially a carnivorous animal that eats dead animals rather than or in addition to hunting live prey.

words.ex: The police scotched the plan to rob the bank.
words.ex_cn: 警察阻止了抢劫银行的计划。
words.en: To scotch something means to stop it from continuing or developing.

words.ex: She scoured the pan until it was clean.
words.ex_cn: 她把锅擦得干干净净。
words.en: If you scour something, you clean it by rubbing it hard with something rough.

words.ex: There was a scramble for the last ticket.
words.ex_cn: 大家争相抢购最后一张票。
words.en: If you scramble over rocks or up a hill, you move quickly over them or up it using your hands to help you. Scramble can also mean to compete or struggle with others for something that is in short supply.

words.tr:
n. 顾虑；顾忌；踌躇
v. 顾虑；有顾忌
words.ex: He had a scruple about lying to his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他对于对朋友撒谎感到不安。
words.en: A scruple is a feeling of doubt or hesitation with regard to the morality or propriety of a course of action.

words.ex: He went diving with scuba gear.
words.ex_cn: 他带着水肺去潜水。
words.en: Scuba is an apparatus containing compressed air and used for breathing underwater, typically consisting of a mouthpiece, a demand valve, and one or more tanks of compressed air.

words.tr:
n. 调味品；佐料
v. 给 ... 调味；适应；风干；“season”的现在分词
words.ex: She added seasoning to the soup.
words.ex_cn: 她给汤里加了调味料。
words.en: Seasoning is a substance that is added to food to improve its flavor.

words.ex: He lives in seclusion in the mountains.
words.ex_cn: 他住在山里，过着与世隔绝的生活。
words.en: The state of being private and away from other people.

words.ex: The gland secrete sweat to cool the body.
words.ex_cn: 腺体分泌汗液来降温。
words.en: If part of a plant, animal, or human secretes a liquid or substance, it produces it.

words.ex: The sect held unusual beliefs that differed from the main religion.
words.ex_cn: 这个派别的信仰与主流宗教不同。
words.en: A sect is a group of people who have different religious beliefs from other people in the same religion.

words.tr: adj. 世俗的；非宗教的；长期的
words.ex: He lives a secular life without religion.
words.ex_cn: 他过着没有宗教的世俗生活。
words.en: Secular activities, attitudes, or things have no connection with religion.

words.tr: adj. 需要久坐的；惯于久坐不动的；不爱活动的；
words.ex: His sedentary job makes him sit all day.
words.ex_cn: 他的久坐工作让他整天坐着。
words.en: Someone who has a sedentary lifestyle or job sits down a lot of the time and does not take much exercise.

words.ex: Rivers carry sediment to the sea.
words.ex_cn: 河流把沉积物带到大海。
words.en: Material that settles to the bottom of a liquid; matter that has been deposited by some natural process.

words.ex: He tried to seduce her with flowers and gifts.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用鲜花和礼物引诱她。
words.en: To seduce someone means to persuade them to do something, especially something wrong or unwise, by making it seem attractive or exciting.

words.ex: The gardener planted a seedling in the garden.
words.ex_cn: 园丁在花园里种了一株幼苗。
words.en: A seedling is a young plant that has grown from a seed.

words.ex: The seismic wave shook the ground.
words.ex_cn: 地震波震动了地面。
words.en: Seismic means relating to or caused by an earthquake or earth vibration.

words.tr: adj. 耸人听闻的；极好的；
words.ex: The newspaper published a sensational story about a ghost.
words.ex_cn: 这家报纸刊登了一篇关于幽灵的耸人听闻的消息。
words.en: A sensational event or situation is so remarkable that it causes great excitement and interest.

words.ex: The sensory experience of eating chocolate is wonderful.
words.ex_cn: 吃巧克力的感觉体验很棒。
words.en: Sensory means relating to the physical senses of touch, smell, taste, hearing, and sight.

words.tr:
adj. 锯齿状的；有锯齿的
v. 使成锯齿状；“serrate”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: The blade of the knife was serrated for cutting bread.
words.ex_cn: 这把刀的刀刃是锯齿状的，适合切面包。
words.en: Having a row of small sharp projections along the edge like a saw.

words.ex: The city improved its sewerage system last year.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市去年改进了其排水系统。
words.en: The system of removing waste water and human excrement from homes and other buildings, and the waste material that is removed.

words.ex: The sword slid easily into its sheath.
words.ex_cn: 剑很容易地滑入鞘中。
words.en: A sheath is a close-fitting cover for the blade of a knife or sword, or a similar protective covering for something else.

words.ex: He shivered in the cold wind.
words.ex_cn: 他在寒风中哆嗦。
words.en: If you shiver, your body shakes slightly because you are cold or frightened.

words.ex: He found a shortcut to school.
words.ex_cn: 他找到了一条去学校的捷径。
words.en: A quicker or more direct way to get somewhere or do something.

words.ex: The child let out a loud shriek when she saw the spider.
words.ex_cn: 当孩子看到蜘蛛时，发出了一声大叫。
words.en: If someone shrieks, they make a short, very loud cry, for example because they are suddenly surprised, are in pain, or are laughing.

words.ex: The apple shrivels in the sun.
words.ex_cn: 苹果在阳光下皱缩。
words.en: If something shrivels or if you shrivel it, it becomes dryer and smaller, often with lines in its surface, as a result of losing the water it contains.

words.ex: The shrub grows near the fence.
words.ex_cn: 这丛灌木长在篱笆附近。
words.en: A shrub is a woody plant which is smaller than a tree and has several main stems arising at or near the ground.

words.tr:
v. 拖曳；搅乱；洗牌；移来移去
n. 拖着脚走；洗牌；混在一起
words.ex: He shuffle his feet across the floor.
words.ex_cn: 他拖着脚在地板上走。
words.en: To shuffle is to walk by dragging one's feet along or without lifting them fully from the ground. It also means to mix up the order of things, especially cards in a deck.

words.tr:
v. 向旁侧避让；回避
n. 向侧方跨步
words.ex: He sidestepped the question during the interview.
words.ex_cn: 他在采访中回避了这个问题。
words.en: If you sidestep a problem or question, you avoid answering it or dealing with it.

words.ex: His silly hat made everyone laugh.
words.ex_cn: 他那可笑的帽子让大家都笑了。
words.en: If you say that someone or something is silly, you mean that they are foolish, childish, or ridiculous.

words.ex: The river deposited silt on the banks.
words.ex_cn: 河流在河岸上沉积了淤泥。
words.en: Silt is fine sand, soil, or mud which is carried along by a river and then left on the land.

words.ex: The simplicity of the design makes it easy to use.
words.ex_cn: 这种设计的简单使它容易使用。
words.en: The quality or condition of being easy to understand or do.

words.ex: The river has a sinuous path through the forest.
words.ex_cn: 这条河在森林中蜿蜒流淌。
words.en: Something that is sinuous has many smooth turns and curves.

words.tr: v. 舍不得给；节省；克扣
words.ex: She skimped on the ingredients to save money.
words.ex_cn: 她为了省钱，在食材上克扣。
words.en: To skimp means to spend less time, money, or effort on something than is really needed, often resulting in a lower quality outcome.

words.tr:
n. 冲天火箭
v. 剧增；猛涨；猛升
words.ex: The price of housing skyrocketed last year.
words.ex_cn: 去年房价急剧上涨。
words.en: To increase very quickly and suddenly.

words.tr:
n. 平板；厚板；厚片
v. 切成厚板
words.ex: He broke the slab of concrete with a hammer.
words.ex_cn: 他用锤子砸碎了那块混凝土板。
words.en: A slab is a thick, flat piece of a hard material such as stone, concrete, or wood.

words.tr:
v. 诋毁；诽谤；中伤
n. 诋毁；诽谤；中伤
words.ex: He spread slander about his neighbor.
words.ex_cn: 他散布了关于他邻居的诽谤。
words.en: Slander is the action or crime of making a false spoken statement damaging to a person's reputation.

words.tr:
n. 砍痕；伤痕；斜线号；削减
v. 砍；大幅度削减
words.ex: The tree has a deep slash on its trunk.
words.ex_cn: 这棵树的树干上有一道深深的砍痕。
words.en: To cut something with a sharp object in a violent way; to reduce something by a large amount suddenly.

words.ex: The slime at the bottom of the river smells bad.
words.ex_cn: 河底的污泥闻起来很难闻。
words.en: Slime is a thick, wet, slippery substance, often unpleasant to touch.

words.ex: The floor is slippery after it rains.
words.ex_cn: 下雨后地板很滑。
words.en: Something that is slippery is smooth, wet, or oily and is therefore difficult to walk on or to hold.

words.ex: The sloth moves very slowly in the tree.
words.ex_cn: 树懒在树上移动得非常慢。
words.en: Sloth is a disinclination to work or exert oneself; laziness, or a slow-moving tropical American mammal that lives in trees.

words.ex: The turtle moves in a sluggish way.
words.ex_cn: 乌龟移动得很缓慢。
words.en: If you describe something as sluggish, you mean that it is moving or working more slowly than usual.

words.tr: adj. 诡诈的；诡秘的；心照不宣的
words.ex: The sly fox stole the chicken at night.
words.ex_cn: 那只狡猾的狐狸在夜里偷了鸡。
words.en: Someone who is sly is clever and good at deceiving people in a way that is not easily noticed.

words.tr: n. 熔炼；冶炼； v. “smelt”的现在分词；
words.ex: The factory uses smelting to extract metal from ore.
words.ex_cn: 工厂使用熔炼从矿石中提取金属。
words.en: The process of extracting a metal from its ore by heating and melting.

words.ex: The city has heavy smog in winter.
words.ex_cn: 这个城市冬天有严重的雾霾。
words.en: Smog is a mixture of smoke and fog, or a similar mixture of air pollutants, which can be harmful to health.

words.tr: v. 厚厚地覆盖；使…窒息；闷死
words.ex: He tried to smother the fire with a blanket.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用毯子把火闷灭。
words.en: To smother someone or something means to kill them by covering their face so that they cannot breathe, or to put out a fire by covering it.

words.tr: n. 小片；小部分；零星片段
words.ex: He shared a snippet of his new song.
words.ex_cn: 他分享了他新歌的一小段。
words.en: A snippet is a small piece of something, especially a piece of information or a short extract from a piece of writing or music.

words.tr: adj. 势利的；谄上欺下的
words.ex: He is snobbish and ignores people who are not rich.
words.ex_cn: 他很势利，不理睬不富有的人。
words.en: If you describe someone as snobbish, you disapprove of them because they are too proud of their social status, intelligence, or taste.

words.ex: A snowflake falls gently from the sky.
words.ex_cn: 一片雪花轻轻从天空飘落。
words.en: A snowflake is a single ice crystal that has achieved a sufficient size, and may have amalgamated with others, which falls through the Earth's atmosphere as snow.

words.ex: He is a sociable man who likes to talk with friends.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个喜欢和朋友聊天的外向的人。
words.en: A sociable person is friendly and enjoys being with other people.

words.tr:
n. 焊料；焊锡
v. 焊接；焊合
words.ex: He used solder to fix the broken wire.
words.ex_cn: 他用焊料修理了断掉的电线。
words.en: Solder is a fusible metal alloy used to create a permanent bond between metal workpieces.

words.tr: v. 恳求；征求；（妓女）拉客
words.ex: He solicits donations for the charity.
words.ex_cn: 他为慈善机构募捐。
words.en: If you solicit money, help, support, or an opinion from someone, you ask them for it.

words.tr: v. 使安静；安慰；使缓和
words.ex: She sang a song to soothe the baby.
words.ex_cn: 她唱了一首歌来安抚婴儿。
words.en: To soothe someone means to make them feel calmer and less anxious, upset, or angry.

words.tr:
adj. 隔音的
v. 使隔音
words.ex: He put soundproof foam on the walls.
words.ex_cn: 他在墙上安装了隔音泡沫。
words.en: Soundproof refers to something that is designed to prevent sound from entering or leaving a place.

words.ex: I bought a souvenir from the beach.
words.ex_cn: 我从海边买了一个纪念品。
words.en: A souvenir is something which you buy or keep to remind you of a holiday, place, or event.

words.ex: The spaceship flew to the moon.
words.ex_cn: 宇宙飞船飞到了月球。
words.en: A spacecraft designed for travel or operation in outer space.

words.ex: The village has a sparse population.
words.ex_cn: 这个村庄人口稀少。
words.en: Something that is sparse is small in number or amount and spread out over an area.

words.ex: The fish spawn in the river each spring.
words.ex_cn: 鱼每年春天在河里产卵。
words.en: To spawn means to produce or deposit eggs, especially in large quantities, as fish, frogs, etc. do. It can also mean to give rise to or generate something.

words.ex: The warrior threw a spear at the enemy.
words.ex_cn: 战士向敌人投掷了一支矛。
words.en: A spear is a weapon consisting of a long pole with a sharp point at one end, used for thrusting or throwing.

words.tr:
n. 微粒；斑点；少量
v. 使有斑点
words.ex: There is a speck of dust on the table.
words.ex_cn: 桌子上有一粒灰尘。
words.en: A speck is a very small stain, mark, or container of something.

words.tr: adj. 快的；迅速的；敏捷的；
words.ex: He gave a speedy reply to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题做出了快速的答复。
words.en: Something that is speedy moves or happens quickly.

words.ex: The boy hurt his spine when he fell from the tree.
words.ex_cn: 他从树上摔下来时伤到了脊柱。
words.en: The spine is the row of bones down the center of your back that supports your body and protects your spinal cord.

words.tr:
v. 喷吐；吐痰；吐口水
n. 唾沫；一块陆地；烤肉叉
words.ex: He likes to spit watermelon seeds.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢吐西瓜籽。
words.en: To spit means to force out the contents of the mouth, especially saliva, through the lips. It can also refer to the act of ejecting saliva or phlegm from the mouth, often as a gesture of contempt or disrespect.

words.ex: He did it out of spite.
words.ex_cn: 他出于恶意做了这件事。
words.en: If you do something out of spite, you do it because you want to hurt or upset someone.

words.ex: The city's sprawl has covered many farmlands.
words.ex_cn: 这个城市的杂乱无序的拓展覆盖了许多农田。
words.en: If you sprawl somewhere, you sit or lie with your legs and arms spread out in a careless way.

words.tr:
v. 洒；撒；下小雨
n. 洒；撒；小雨；少量
words.ex: She sprinkles sugar on her cereal.
words.ex_cn: 她在麦片上撒糖。
words.en: To scatter or pour small drops or particles of a substance over an object or surface.

words.tr: v. 发芽；长出；迅速成长；涌现；
words.ex: The seed will sprout in spring.
words.ex_cn: 这颗种子会在春天发芽。
words.en: If a plant sprouts, or if it sprouts something, it produces new leaves or buds.

words.tr: adv. 直角地；径直地；公平地；直接了当
words.ex: He stood squarely in front of the door.
words.ex_cn: 他直角地站在门前面。
words.en: If something is squarely placed or aimed, it is placed or aimed directly at something.

words.tr:
n. 球类运动（squash）；
v. 压碎；
words.ex: He plays squash every weekend with his friends.
words.ex_cn: 他每周末和朋友打壁球。
words.en: To squash something means to press or squeeze it so that it becomes flat, soft, or out of shape. It can also refer to the sport of squash or a type of vegetable.

words.ex: The child squirted water from the hose.
words.ex_cn: 孩子从软管里喷出水。
words.en: To squirt means to force out liquid in a thin fast stream or to be forced out in this way.

words.ex: The stagecoach carried passengers across the desert.
words.ex_cn: 驿站马车运送乘客穿越沙漠。
words.en: A stagecoach is a large carriage pulled by horses that was used in the past to carry passengers and mail along a regular route.

words.tr:
n. 茎；柄；梗
v. 跟踪；偷偷接近；昂首阔步地走
words.ex: The stalk of the sunflower is very tall.
words.ex_cn: 向日葵的茎很高。
words.en: The main stem of a plant, typically rising above ground but occasionally subterranean. Also, to pursue or approach stealthily.

words.ex: He has great stamina for running long distances.
words.ex_cn: 他有很强的耐力来跑长距离。
words.en: Stamina is the physical or mental energy needed to do a tiring activity for a long time.

words.tr: v. “stand”的现在分词；站立； adj. 直立的；常设的； n. 地位；
words.ex: He is standing by the door.
words.ex_cn: 他正站在门边。
words.en: Your standing is your status or reputation.

words.ex: The poem has four stanzas.
words.ex_cn: 这首诗有四节。
words.en: A stanza is a group of lines in a poem that are separated from other groups by a space.

words.tr:
adj. 主要的；重要的；
n. 主要产品；主要部分；主食；
words.ex: Rice is a staple food in many Asian countries.
words.ex_cn: 大米是许多亚洲国家的主要食物。
words.en: A staple is a basic food that is eaten regularly and in such quantities that it constitutes a dominant portion of a standard diet for a given people, supplying a large fraction of energy needs and generally forming a significant proportion of the intake of other nutrients as well.

words.tr:
n. 淀粉；淀粉浆
v. 给（布）上浆
words.ex: The potato contains a lot of starch.
words.ex_cn: 土豆含有大量淀粉。
words.en: A carbohydrate that is the chief form of stored energy in plants, especially in seeds and tubers. It is also used in cooking and as a stiffening agent in textiles.

words.ex: He dreams of stardom after winning the talent show.
words.ex_cn: 他在赢得才艺比赛后梦想着成名。
words.en: The status of being a very famous or popular performer, especially in the entertainment industry.

words.tr: adj. 完全的；荒凉的；光秃秃的；僵硬的；严厉的
words.ex: There was a stark difference between the two results.
words.ex_cn: 这两个结果之间有完全的差异。
words.en: Stark means complete, severe, or obvious in a way that is impossible to avoid noticing.

words.tr:
v. 藏匿；隐藏
n. 一批贮藏物
words.ex: He stashes his money under the bed.
words.ex_cn: 他把钱藏在床底下。
words.en: If you stash something valuable in a secret place, you store it there to keep it safe.

words.tr: adj. 庄重的；庄严的；堂皇的；
words.ex: The stately mansion stood on the hill.
words.ex_cn: 那座庄重的豪宅矗立在山上。
words.en: Something that is stately is impressive because of its size, beauty, or grandeur.

words.ex: His stature in the scientific community is very high.
words.ex_cn: 他在科学界声望很高。
words.en: The height of a person or an animal in a standing position; the level of respect that people have for a person or organization because of their importance or success.

words.ex: He is steadfast in his beliefs.
words.ex_cn: 他对自己信念坚定不移。
words.en: If someone is steadfast, they are very loyal and constant in their attitudes or actions.

words.ex: He gave a stellar performance in the play.
words.ex_cn: 他在剧中表现出色。
words.en: Of or relating to stars; outstanding or excellent.

words.tr: adj. 不能生育的；贫瘠的；
words.ex: The doctor said the man is sterile.
words.ex_cn: 医生说这个人不能生育。
words.en: Something that is sterile is completely clean and free from bacteria or other microorganisms.

words.ex: The smoke began to stifle her breathing.
words.ex_cn: 烟雾开始让她窒息。
words.en: To stifle something means to prevent it from happening, continuing, or developing.

words.ex: He receives a small stipend for his internship.
words.ex_cn: 他因实习获得少量薪金。
words.en: A stipend is a sum of money paid regularly as a salary or allowance.

words.ex: The contract stipulates that payments must be made monthly.
words.ex_cn: 合同规定付款必须按月进行。
words.en: If you stipulate a condition or stipulate that something must be done, you say clearly that it must be done.

words.ex: He is a stocky man with strong arms.
words.ex_cn: 他是个身材敦实、手臂强壮的人。
words.en: A stocky person is broad and solidly built.

words.ex: The old tree has a stout trunk.
words.ex_cn: 这棵老树有一个粗壮的树干。
words.en: Someone who is stout is rather fat or heavy.

words.tr:
v. 使滞留；使搁浅；
n. 方面；
words.ex: The storm stranded the travelers on the island.
words.ex_cn: 风暴使旅行者滞留在岛上。
words.en: If someone is stranded, they are left in a place that is difficult for them to get away from. A strand of something such as hair, wire, or thread is a single thin piece of it.

words.tr: n. 岩层；地层；社会阶层；“stratum”的复数
words.ex: The geologist studied the strata in the cliff.
words.ex_cn: 地质学家研究了悬崖中的岩层。
words.en: In geology, strata are layers of rock, and in sociology, strata refer to the divisions within society based on factors such as wealth, power, and education.

words.ex: Hiking up the mountain was a strenuous task.
words.ex_cn: 爬山是一项艰苦的任务。
words.en: Requiring or using great effort or exertion.

words.ex: The school has stringent rules about homework.
words.ex_cn: 学校对作业有严格的规定。
words.en: Stringent measures, rules, or conditions are very strict or severe.

words.ex: The room was stuffy and hard to breathe in.
words.ex_cn: 房间闷热得让人难以呼吸。
words.en: If you describe a place as stuffy, you mean that it is unpleasantly warm and has no fresh air.

words.tr: adj. 极好的；令人震惊的； v. “stun”的现在分词；
words.ex: She wore a stunning dress to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一件极好的裙子去参加派对。
words.en: Extremely impressive or attractive.

words.tr: n. 特技表演；噱头；发育不良的动植物；
words.ex: The actor performed a dangerous stunt in the movie.
words.ex_cn: 这位演员在电影中表演了一个危险的特技。
words.en: A stunt is a dangerous feat that is done to entertain people, especially in a film.

words.ex: The ground began to subside after the heavy rain.
words.ex_cn: 大雨之后，地面开始下陷。
words.en: If a feeling or noise subsides, it becomes less strong or loud.

words.tr: v. 维持生活；生存下去
words.ex: They subsist on rice and vegetables.
words.ex_cn: 他们靠米饭和蔬菜维持生活。
words.en: If people subsist, they are just able to obtain the food or money that they need in order to stay alive.

words.ex: He needs to substantiate his claim with evidence.
words.ex_cn: 他需要用证据来证实他的说法。
words.en: To substantiate a statement or a story means to supply evidence which proves that it is true.

words.tr: adj. 本质上的；实质性的；
words.ex: The change was substantive, not just cosmetic.
words.ex_cn: 这个改变是本质上的，而不仅仅是表面上的。
words.en: Something that is substantive is significant, meaningful, or important in a way that is not just superficial or formal.

words.ex: The subterranean tunnel connects two buildings.
words.ex_cn: 这条地下的隧道连接着两栋大楼。
words.en: Existing, occurring, or done under the earth's surface.

words.tr:
adj. 颠覆性的；破坏性的
n. 颠覆分子；危险分子
words.ex: The subversive poster tried to break the government's rules.
words.ex_cn: 那张颠覆性的海报试图破坏政府的规则。
words.en: A subversive person or activity is one that is intended to weaken or destroy a political system or government.

words.ex: He gave a succinct answer.
words.ex_cn: 他给出了一个简洁的回答。
words.en: Something that is succinct expresses facts or ideas clearly and in few words.

words.ex: He succumbed to the illness after a long fight.
words.ex_cn: 经过长期抗争后，他最终死于疾病。
words.en: If you succumb to temptation, pressure, or something such as an illness, you do something that you want to do, or you give in to the pressure or illness, often after a period of trying not to.

words.ex: The king ate a sumptuous meal in his palace.
words.ex_cn: 国王在他的宫殿里享用了一顿丰盛的饭菜。
words.en: Something that is sumptuous is very impressive and expensive, especially in a way that involves large amounts of money.

words.ex: Plants grow better with sunlight.
words.ex_cn: 植物在阳光下生长得更好。
words.en: Sunlight is the light that comes from the sun.

words.ex: The extra words are superfluous.
words.ex_cn: 这些额外的词是多余的。
words.en: Something that is superfluous is unnecessary or no longer needed.

words.ex: The superintendent of the school is very strict.
words.ex_cn: 学校的主管非常严格。
words.en: A superintendent is a person who is in charge of a particular department or activity, especially within a school, housing project, or police force.

words.ex: The movie shows a supernatural ghost.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影展示了一个超自然的幽灵。
words.en: Relating to phenomena that cannot be explained by natural laws and are therefore attributed to a divine agency.

words.ex: Smartphones supplanted landline phones.
words.ex_cn: 智能手机取代了固定电话。
words.en: To supplant someone or something means to take the place of them, often by being more powerful or effective.

words.tr: adj. 柔软的；灵活的；思维敏捷的
words.ex: The yoga teacher has supple legs.
words.ex_cn: 瑜伽老师腿很柔软。
words.en: A supple object or material bends or changes shape easily without breaking or cracking.

words.tr:
n. 额外费用；附加费
v. 额外索价；附加罚款
words.ex: He paid a surcharge for extra baggage.
words.ex_cn: 他为额外行李支付了附加费。
words.en: An additional charge or payment.

words.ex: He surmounted his fears to speak in public.
words.ex_cn: 他克服了恐惧，在公众面前发言。
words.en: If you surmount a problem or difficulty, you deal successfully with it.

words.tr: n. 食物；营养；维持生计
words.ex: Water and food are basic sustenance for life.
words.ex_cn: 水和食物是生命的基本生存物资。
words.en: Sustenance refers to the food and drink that people, animals, and plants need to live and stay healthy. It can also mean the means of maintaining life or supporting existence.

words.ex: The word 'cat' has one syllable.
words.ex_cn: 单词 'cat' 有一个音节。
words.en: A syllable is a unit of organization for a sequence of speech sounds. It is typically made up of a syllable nucleus (most often a vowel) with optional initial and final margins (typically, consonants).

words.ex: Bees and flowers have symbiosis.
words.ex_cn: 蜜蜂和花朵之间有共生关系。
words.en: Symbiosis is a close relationship between two different kinds of living things in which each provides something that the other needs.

words.tr: v. 象征；代表；用符号表示
words.ex: The dove symbolizes peace.
words.ex_cn: 鸽子象征和平。
words.en: If one thing symbolizes another, it is used or regarded as a symbol of it.

words.ex: The butterfly is symmetrical.
words.ex_cn: 这只蝴蝶是对称的。
words.en: Something that is symmetrical has parts that are equal in size, shape, and position, and that are arranged in a balanced way.

words.ex: The synonym of 'happy' is 'glad'.
words.ex_cn: ‘happy’的同义词是‘glad’。
words.en: A synonym is a word or phrase that means exactly or nearly the same as another word or phrase in the same language.

words.ex: He tries to synthesize ideas from different books.
words.ex_cn: 他试图综合来自不同书籍的想法。
words.en: To synthesize means to combine different ideas, influences, or objects into a new whole, or to produce a substance by a chemical reaction in plants or animals.

words.ex: He poured syrup on his pancakes.
words.ex_cn: 他把糖浆倒在煎饼上。
words.en: A thick, sweet liquid made by dissolving sugar in boiling water, often used as a topping for desserts or as a sweetener in drinks.

words.ex: The tableland is known for its rich mineral deposits.
words.ex_cn: 这片高原以其丰富的矿藏而闻名。
words.en: A tableland is a large flat area of land that is higher than the land around it.

words.ex: It is a taboo to speak his name in this village.
words.ex_cn: 在这个村子里，提到他的名字是禁忌。
words.en: A taboo is a social or religious custom prohibiting or restricting a particular practice or forbidding association with a particular person, place, or thing.

words.tr: adj. 触觉的；能触知的；手感好的
words.ex: The child learns through tactile objects like blocks.
words.ex_cn: 孩子通过触觉物体如积木来学习。
words.en: Relating to the sense of touch; perceptible by touch.

words.tr:
n. 标签；标记；
v. 加标签于；
words.ex: The tag on the shirt says 'wash cold'.
words.ex_cn: 衬衫上的标签写着‘冷水洗涤’。
words.en: A tag is a small piece of card, cloth, or plastic which is attached to an object or person and has information about that object or person on it. A tag can also be a word or phrase that is used to describe or identify something, especially in a computer file or on a website.

words.tr:
n. 污染；腐坏；玷污
v. 污染；使腐坏；玷污
words.ex: The water has a taint from the factory waste.
words.ex_cn: 这种水因工厂废料而受到污染。
words.en: If something is tainted, it is affected by something bad or undesirable.

words.ex: He is a talkative boy who loves to tell stories.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个爱说话的男孩，喜欢讲故事。
words.en: A talkative person talks a lot.

words.tr:
n. 记数；
v. 合计；
words.ex: He kept a tally of how many goals he scored.
words.ex_cn: 他记录了自己进了多少球。
words.en: A tally is a record of amounts or numbers which you keep changing and adding to as the activity which affects it progresses.

words.tr: adj. 迟的；缓慢的；迟缓的
words.ex: He is tardy for school every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上上学都迟到。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as tardy, you think that they are later than they should be or later than expected.

words.tr:
v. （使）失去光泽；使晦暗；玷污
n. 晦暗；污渍
words.ex: The silver spoon will tarnish if not cleaned.
words.ex_cn: 如果银勺不清洗，就会变暗。
words.en: If you say that something tarnishes someone's reputation or image, you mean that it causes people to have a worse opinion of them than they would otherwise have had.

words.ex: He drank beer in a small tavern.
words.ex_cn: 他在一家小酒馆里喝啤酒。
words.en: A tavern is a place where alcoholic drinks are served and people gather to drink and socialize.

words.ex: He studies tectonics to understand how buildings are constructed.
words.ex_cn: 他研究筑造学以了解建筑物是如何建造的。
words.en: Tectonics is the study of the Earth's structural features, especially the folding and faulting of the Earth's crust.

words.tr:
n. 媒介；方法；
adj. 中等的；适中的；
words.ex: TV is a popular medium for advertising.
words.ex_cn: 电视是一种流行的广告媒介。
words.en: A medium is a method or way of expressing something.

words.ex: He is a temperate person who never shouts.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个温和的人，从不大喊大叫。
words.en: If you describe someone's behavior as temperate, you mean that it is calm and reasonable, not extreme or emotional.

words.ex: Many families live in a small tenement in the city.
words.ex_cn: 许多家庭住在城市里的一间廉价公寓里。
words.en: A tenement is a large old building which is divided into a number of individual flats.

words.ex: The octopus used its tentacle to catch the fish.
words.ex_cn: 章鱼用它的触角抓到了鱼。
words.en: A tentacle is a long, flexible arm or limb of an animal, especially one used for grasping or feeling.

words.ex: The doctor used medical terminology to explain the illness.
words.ex_cn: 医生使用医学术语来解释这种疾病。
words.en: The set of terms and expressions used in a particular subject, field, or profession.

words.ex: The train stops at the terminus.
words.ex_cn: 火车在终点站停下。
words.en: A terminus is the end of a transportation line or the station at the end of a railway or bus route.

words.ex: The termite ate the wooden table.
words.ex_cn: 白蚁吃掉了木桌子。
words.en: A termite is a small, pale soft-bodied insect that lives in large colonies with several different castes, typically within a mound of cemented earth. Termites feed on wood and can cause extensive damage to buildings and other wooden structures.

words.ex: The terrestrial animals live on land.
words.ex_cn: 陆地动物生活在陆地上。
words.en: Of, on, or relating to the earth.

words.tr:
v. 使融解；解冻；变缓和
n. 融雪
words.ex: The ice begins to thaw in spring.
words.ex_cn: 冰在春天开始融化。
words.en: If ice, snow, or something else that is frozen thaws, it melts. A thaw is a period of warmer weather when snow and ice melt, usually at the end of winter.

words.ex: He hurt his thigh while running.
words.ex_cn: 他跑步时伤了大腿。
words.en: The part of the human leg between the hip and the knee.

words.ex: She is thrifty and saves money every week.
words.ex_cn: 她很节约，每周都存钱。
words.en: If you say that someone is thrifty, you are praising them for saving money and not spending it on unnecessary things.

words.ex: The thunderstorm woke us up at night.
words.ex_cn: 雷雨在夜里把我们吵醒了。
words.en: A thunderstorm is a storm with thunder and lightning and typically also heavy rain or hail.

words.ex: She tinted the glass blue.
words.ex_cn: 她把玻璃染成了蓝色。
words.en: A tint is a small amount of a particular color, especially when it is used to make the main color lighter or darker.

words.ex: The map shows the topography of the mountain area.
words.ex_cn: 这张地图显示了山区的地形。
words.en: The topography of an area is the physical features of its surface, such as hills, valleys, and rivers, especially the representation of these features on maps.

words.ex: Farmers protect the topsoil to grow healthy crops.
words.ex_cn: 农民保护表土以种植健康的作物。
words.en: Topsoil is the upper layer of soil, usually the top 2 inches (5.1 cm) to 8 inches (20 cm). It has the highest concentration of organic matter and microorganisms and is where most of the Earth's biological soil activity occurs.

words.ex: He used a torch to find his keys in the dark.
words.ex_cn: 他用手电筒在黑暗中找钥匙。
words.en: A torch is a stick with a flame on one end that is used as a source of light, or a portable battery-powered electric lamp.

words.ex: The tornado destroyed the small house.
words.ex_cn: 龙卷风摧毁了那座小房子。
words.en: A tornado is a violent windstorm characterized by a twisting, funnel-shaped cloud.

words.ex: The cold weather put the animal into torpor.
words.ex_cn: 寒冷的天气让动物陷入麻木状态。
words.en: a state of physical or mental inactivity; lethargy.

words.ex: The rain caused a torrent down the mountain.
words.ex_cn: 大雨在山间形成了一股急流。
words.en: A torrent is a fast-moving stream of water or other liquid.

words.ex: The tortuous road wound through the mountains.
words.ex_cn: 这条弯曲的道路蜿蜒穿过山脉。
words.en: If you describe something as tortuous, you mean that it is very long, complicated, and difficult to understand.

words.tr: v. 触摸；接触；“touch”的现在分词；
words.ex: The child is touching the soft blanket.
words.ex_cn: 孩子在触摸柔软的毯子。
words.en: If something is touching, it causes feelings of sadness or sympathy.

words.ex: He won the chess tournament last week.
words.ex_cn: 他上周赢得了国际象棋锦标赛。
words.en: A tournament is a competition in which players who win a match continue to play further matches in the competition until just one person or team is left.

words.tr: adj. 高耸的；杰出的；激烈的； v. “tower”的现在分词；
words.ex: The towering building stood above all others in the city.
words.ex_cn: 那座高耸的建筑矗立在城市中所有其他建筑之上。
words.en: Very tall or high; outstanding or extreme.

words.ex: The water is toxic to fish.
words.ex_cn: 这种水对鱼是有毒的。
words.en: If a substance is toxic, it is poisonous.

words.tr:
n. 流浪汉；流浪乞丐；徒步旅行
v. 步行；踩；踏
words.ex: The old tramp slept on the park bench.
words.ex_cn: 那个老流浪汉睡在公园的长椅上。
words.en: If you tramp somewhere, you walk there slowly and with regular, heavy steps, especially for a long time.

words.ex: The cows trample the grass in the field.
words.ex_cn: 牛在田野里践踏草地。
words.en: If someone tramples something or tramples on it, they step heavily and carelessly on it and damage it.

words.tr: adj. 安静的；平静的；宁静的；
words.ex: The lake was tranquil in the morning.
words.ex_cn: 早晨的湖面很安静。
words.en: If a place or situation is tranquil, it is calm, peaceful, and quiet, with no disturbance or agitation.

words.ex: She transcended her fears to speak on stage.
words.ex_cn: 她超越了自己的恐惧，在舞台上发言。
words.en: If something transcends normal limits or boundaries, it goes beyond them, because it is more significant than them.

words.ex: The glass is translucent, so you can see light through it.
words.ex_cn: 这种玻璃是半透明的，所以你能看到光透过它。
words.en: If a material or substance is translucent, it is almost transparent, allowing some light to pass through it but not detailed shapes.

words.ex: The wizard can transmute lead into gold.
words.ex_cn: 巫师可以把铅变成金子。
words.en: To change something completely, especially into something different and better.

words.tr: n. 垃圾；无价值的东西；
words.ex: The trash bin is full.
words.ex_cn: 垃圾桶满了。
words.en: Waste material or unwanted things that are thrown away.

words.ex: The treacherous road made driving very scary.
words.ex_cn: 这条危险的道路让驾驶非常可怕。
words.en: If you describe someone as treacherous, you mean that they are likely to betray you and cannot be trusted. If you say that something is treacherous, you mean that it is very dangerous and unpredictable.

words.tr:
v. 踩；踏；践踏
n. 脚步声；胎面
words.ex: He tread carefully on the icy path.
words.ex_cn: 他小心地走在结冰的小路上。
words.en: If you tread on something, you put your foot on it when you are walking. The tread of a tyre is the pattern of lines on its surface that prevent it from slipping.

words.ex: He was punished for treason against the king.
words.ex_cn: 他因对国王叛国而受到惩罚。
words.en: Treason is the crime of betraying your country, for example by helping its enemies or by trying to remove its government using violence.

words.tr:
v. 非法侵入；侵扰；冒犯
n. 非法进入；冒犯
words.ex: He trespasses on private land.
words.ex_cn: 他擅自进入私人土地。
words.en: To trespass is to enter someone's land or property without their permission.

words.ex: The small river flows into the main river as a tributary.
words.ex_cn: 这条小河作为支流汇入主河。
words.en: A tributary is a stream or river that flows into a larger stream or main stem (or parent) river or a lake. A tributary does not flow directly into a sea or ocean.

words.tr:
v. 滴流；慢慢移动
n. 细流；徐徐地流
words.ex: Water trickles down the mountain.
words.ex_cn: 水从山上缓缓流下。
words.en: If a liquid trickles somewhere, it flows slowly in a thin stream.

words.ex: He watched the Harry Potter trilogy last weekend.
words.ex_cn: 他上周末看了《哈利·波特》三部曲。
words.en: A trilogy is a series of three books, plays, or films that have the same subject or the same characters.

words.ex: The troupe performed a dance show in the town square.
words.ex_cn: 这个表演团在广场上演了一出舞蹈表演。
words.en: A troupe is a group of actors, singers, or dancers who work together.

words.ex: He is a trustworthy friend who always keeps his promises.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个值得信赖的朋友，总是信守承诺。
words.en: If you describe someone as trustworthy, you mean they are reliable, honest, and truthful.

words.ex: He drove on the turnpike to save time.
words.ex_cn: 他走收费公路以节省时间。
words.en: A turnpike is a road that drivers must pay to use, especially in the past. It is also a gate or barrier set across a road to stop traffic until a toll is paid.

words.ex: A bird built a nest on a small twig.
words.ex_cn: 一只鸟在一根小嫩枝上筑了巢。
words.en: A twig is a very small thin branch that grows out from a main branch of a tree or bush.

words.tr:
n. 合股绳；捻线；麻绳
v. 缠绕；盘绕；使缠结
words.ex: He tied the box with twine.
words.ex_cn: 他用麻绳绑住了盒子。
words.en: Twine refers to a strong thread or string consisting of two or more strands twisted together. It can also mean to twist or wind something around something else.

words.tr: n. 大亨；巨头；大企业家；
words.ex: He became a tycoon after building a big oil company.
words.ex_cn: 他在建立了一家大型石油公司后成为了一位大亨。
words.en: A tycoon is a person who is successful in business or industry and has become rich and powerful.

words.tr: adj. 暴虐的；压制的；残暴的
words.ex: The tyrannical king punished people for small mistakes.
words.ex_cn: 这个暴虐的国王因为小错误惩罚人民。
words.en: Using power in a cruel and unfair way over people in a country or group.

words.ex: He gave an ultimatum: leave now or stay forever.
words.ex_cn: 他发出最后通牒：现在走，或者永远留下。
words.en: An ultimatum is a final demand or statement of terms, the rejection of which will result in retaliation or a breakdown in relations.

words.ex: The doctor used ultrasonic waves to check the baby.
words.ex_cn: 医生使用超声波来检查婴儿。
words.en: Ultrasonic refers to sound waves with frequencies higher than the upper limit of human hearing.

words.tr: n. 一致同意；全体赞同
words.ex: The team showed unanimity in voting for the new plan.
words.ex_cn: 团队在投票支持新计划时意见一致。
words.en: Unanimity is complete agreement among all members of a group.

words.ex: The judge gave an unbiased decision.
words.ex_cn: 法官作出了无偏见的判决。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as unbiased, you mean they are fair and not likely to support one particular person or group involved in something.

words.tr: adj. 不能架桥的；不可逾越的；无法弥合的
words.ex: The gap between them was unbridgeable.
words.ex_cn: 他们之间的鸿沟是无法跨越的。
words.en: If a gap or difference is unbridgeable, it is so large or so great that it cannot be bridged or made any smaller.

words.tr: adj. 无辔头的；不受控制的；放纵的
words.ex: The unbridled horse ran across the field.
words.ex_cn: 那匹无辔头的马在田野上奔跑。
words.en: If you describe behaviour or feelings as unbridled, you mean that they are not controlled or limited in any way.

words.tr: adj. 未破的；不间断的；未驯服的（马）
words.ex: The unbroken chain of events led to the accident.
words.ex_cn: 这一连串未被打断的事件导致了事故。
words.en: If something is unbroken, it is continuous or complete and has not been interrupted or damaged.

words.ex: The country has an underdeveloped economy.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家经济不发达。
words.en: An underdeveloped country or region is one that is less developed economically and socially than most others, with many of its people living in poverty.

words.ex: He is an undergraduate at Harvard.
words.ex_cn: 他是哈佛大学的一名本科生。
words.en: An undergraduate is a student at a university or college who is studying for their first degree.

words.ex: The teacher underscored the importance of homework.
words.ex_cn: 老师强调了作业的重要性。
words.en: To emphasize the importance of something or to draw a line underneath a word or phrase.

words.tr: n. 保证；事业； v. 承担；从事；“undertake”的现在分词；
words.ex: He gave an undertaking to finish the project on time.
words.ex_cn: 他保证按时完成项目。
words.en: An undertaking is a task or project, especially one that is important or difficult.

words.tr:
adv. 在水下；
adj. 水下的；
words.ex: The divers swam underwater to explore the coral reef.
words.ex_cn: 潜水员在水下游泳以探索珊瑚礁。
words.en: Located, occurring, or used beneath the surface of the water.

words.ex: I clicked the button to undo my mistake.
words.ex_cn: 我点击了按钮来撤销我的错误。
words.en: To undo something means to reverse the effect of a previous action or to untie or unfasten something.

words.ex: They unearthed an old coin in the garden.
words.ex_cn: 他们在花园里挖出了一枚旧硬币。
words.en: To unearth something means to find it by digging in the ground or to discover something that was hidden or unknown.

words.tr: adj. 不公正的；不公平的；
words.ex: The teacher gave an unfair test.
words.ex_cn: 老师给了一个不公正的考试。
words.en: If you describe a situation or action as unfair, you mean that it is not right or reasonable, especially because it does not treat people equally.

words.ex: Her skills are unmatched in the team.
words.ex_cn: 她的技能在团队中无人能及。
words.en: If you describe something as unmatched, you are emphasizing that it is better or greater than all other things of the same kind.

words.ex: He unpacks his bags after arriving home.
words.ex_cn: 他到家后打开行李。
words.en: To unpack means to open and remove the contents of a container, such as a suitcase or a box, or to explain or analyze something in detail.

words.ex: The storm caused unprecedented damage.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴造成了前所未有的破坏。
words.en: If something is unprecedented, it has never happened before.

words.ex: He unraveled the knotted string.
words.ex_cn: 他把打结的绳子拆散了。
words.en: To unravel means to separate or disentangle the threads of a fabric or a rope, or to solve or explain something that is complicated or mysterious.

words.tr: adj. 无节制的；不受约束的
words.ex: The child ran unrestrained through the park.
words.ex_cn: 孩子在公园里无拘无束地奔跑。
words.en: If you describe someone's behaviour as unrestrained, you mean that it is extreme or intense because it is not controlled in any way.

words.ex: He made an unscrupulous deal to save money.
words.ex_cn: 他为了省钱做了不道德的交易。
words.en: If you describe someone as unscrupulous, you are critical of them because they are prepared to act in a dishonest or immoral way in order to get what they want.

words.ex: He gave an unsophisticated answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了一个不老练的回答。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as unsophisticated, you mean that they are simple and not complicated, often in a way that is considered positive because it is natural or honest.

words.tr: adj. 笨重的；难处理的；臃肿的；庞大的
words.ex: The box was unwieldy and hard to carry.
words.ex_cn: 这个盒子又大又笨重，很难搬。
words.en: An unwieldy object is difficult to move or handle because of its size, shape, or weight.

words.ex: The storm caused an upheaval in the town.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴给小镇带来了混乱。
words.en: A very large change in something that often causes confusion or problems.

words.tr:
adj. 竖直的；直立的；
adv. 笔直地；
words.ex: The picture is hanging upright on the wall.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画垂直地挂在墙上。
words.en: If you are sitting or standing upright, you are sitting or standing with your back straight, rather than bending or lying down.

words.ex: The announcement caused an uproar in the town.
words.ex_cn: 这个公告在小镇上引起了轩然大波。
words.en: A loud and impassioned noise or disturbance.

words.tr: v. 连根拔起；迁离；根除；
words.ex: The storm uprooted the old tree.
words.ex_cn: 风暴把那棵老树连根拔起了。
words.en: If you uproot yourself or if you are uprooted, you leave a place where you have lived for a long time and go to live somewhere else.

words.tr:
adj. 颠倒的；乱七八糟的
adv. 颠倒地；乱七八糟地
words.ex: The picture is upside-down.
words.ex_cn: 这张照片是倒着的。
words.en: If something is upside-down, it is in a position in which the part that is usually at the bottom is at the top.

words.tr: adj. 实用的；功利主义的；
words.ex: The chair is utilitarian and comfortable.
words.ex_cn: 这把椅子实用又舒适。
words.en: Utilitarian means relating to or adhering to the belief that the value of a thing or an action is determined by its utility.
